Production in the dump's per-class units for seed 7; population in settlement-weight units (w_size x livability); development = built levels + population units (a display index, not in the GDD).

provinces.name: Băng Tâm
provinces.lore: Red badlands, dry steppe and the first snow mountains meet around the seat of Băng Tâm Các. Herders, well-diggers and the sect's own servants live here, and the land yields little but stone, wool and qi. Disciples drink only the seat's ice-cold well water, and the head keeps a retreat in the hills behind it.

provinces.name: Bình Thủy
provinces.lore: A low green headland of grass and bamboo over the strait, the island's door to the mainland. Its people are ferry hands, rope-makers and innkeepers, many of them born somewhere else, and they live by Bình Thủy Môn's crossing. Every dusk the green lanterns on the sect's mast are lit, and a homesick traveller can read the name of his own village among them.

provinces.name: Củng Tinh
provinces.lore: Open high plain more than a thousand metres up, cut by a river and dotted with mountain lakes. Herders and a few barley farmers live around the abbey of Củng Tinh Quán, which keeps the star-iron mine at Vẫn Tinh. On still nights the star-readers watch Tinh Lạc Hồ, and the herders keep their fires low so as not to spoil the water's stars.

provinces.name: Cửu Cao
provinces.lore: Reed marsh and wet woodland along a slow river, with a little steppe and one bare spur of mountain at the edge. Its people cut reed, net marsh fish and keep the roosts of Cửu Cao Phái, whose cranes are the only sky traffic here. Since 874 the crane riders have also held the holdings the Pivot took from Phá Quân Môn, and the marsh villages pay their dues in reed and fish to the sect rather than to the Pivot's clerks.

provinces.name: Dạ Quang
provinces.lore: Steppe, sand and salt pans run to the coast around the red-earth fort of Dạ Quang Môn. Its riders and horse-breeders guard the caravans they once robbed, and the land yields horses, salt and the pale stone of the night-glowing cups. The broken fortress of Cô Thành stands on its salt pan, a reminder of the Desert Road War.

provinces.name: Hàm Nguyệt
provinces.lore: Birch and pine shore along the western end of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ, where the long lake is calmest. Its people fish, tend pearl beds and cut birch for Hàm Nguyệt Trang, which rules the shore for Tùng Đào Cung. Pearls and spirit fish are its wealth, and every fisher here knows the old saying that the moon in the lake is easier to catch than the one in the sky.

provinces.name: Hồng Đậu
provinces.lore: Coastal rain forest and open grass at the western edge of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, where the forest road comes down to the sea at Hồng Đậu Trang. Its people gather rattan, honey and resin and fish the shallows, and many serve the manor as gardeners and porters without asking what grows in its back courts. Vines of red beans run wild along every path, and children are taught early not to put them in their mouths.

provinces.name: Hồng Lô
provinces.lore: A steep coast of snow, black rock and smoking volcanic slopes around the valley of Hồng Lô Cốc. Few mortals live here beyond the valley's servants and ash-gatherers; the land yields sulphur-yellow ores, hot water and furnace heat. The alchemists still sail out to the volcanic isles whenever they smoke, as they did in 1185.

provinces.name: Lãng Đào
provinces.lore: Low wooded ground at the river mouth around the gate of hulls of Lãng Đào Môn. Its people are ferrymen, rope-tarrers and boat-builders who carry the river trade for Tùng Đào. On the shore stand the wrecked piers of Phá Chu Trấn, whose feuding boatmen were the reason the ferrymen banded together in 790.

provinces.name: Lê Hoa
provinces.lore: Ice fields and the highest rock on the continent rise straight from a cold shore here, with a strip of rimed forest at their foot. The nuns of Lê Hoa Am are nearly the only people, and they live on the cold jade they cut high on the mountain and on the gifts of the villages below. Băng Tâm disciples pass through on their way to climb Lăng Tuyệt Phong before a long seclusion, and since Chúc Long Sơn rumbled in 1199 the hermitage has watched the north.

provinces.name: Lễ Tuyền
provinces.lore: Low grassland by the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ and the gulf, where Lễ Tuyền Phái keeps its spring. Its people farm rice, tend the school's herb beds and carry its wine jars to the boats. Envoys of the Pivot come each year for the wine, and a warm spring nearby is where they are made to wait.

provinces.name: Mục Vân
provinces.lore: A small stretch of coastal grass and steppe around the racing track of Mục Vân Trang. Its people are grooms, riders and herders of the manor's spirit horses. An Earth vein under the pasture is said to be why the manor's foals run faster than any on the plain.

provinces.name: Hòa Thử
provinces.lore: Coastal fields of millet climb from the sea into forested hills and a few bare heights. Its farmers keep the stilted granaries that fed Yên Ba Thành through the winter of 860, and still sell to the city first. The hill above the fields is Thúy Vi's, and its disciples climb it to sit among the trees.

provinces.name: Ẩn Loan
provinces.lore: Open grassland and woods end in cliffs over a narrow hidden cove. The few households live by goats, fishing and saying little to strangers, as they have since the pirates left in 781. A small spirit vein in the grass draws Thúy Vi's herb-gatherers each spring.

provinces.name: Ô Đề
provinces.lore: A long stretch of coastal forest with a few limestone knolls and marshy hollows, under the crow ridge of Ô Đề Thôn. Its people fish, cut oak and feed the crows at the new year. Inland lie the walls of a town whose wells turned salt after the earthquake of 1033.

provinces.name: Lâm Tuyền
provinces.lore: Wooded coastal slopes above the bamboo pipe line of Lâm Tuyền Thôn. Its villagers fish and keep the spring that cured the coughing sickness of 760. The woods above ring with cicadas all summer.

provinces.name: Thu Diệp
provinces.lore: Steep mountain, limestone and maple forest falling to the sea around Thu Diệp Thôn. The village lives by fishing and by the red leaves it sells as bookmarks in Lam Yên Thị. A summit of red maples above it is the source of the best leaves.

provinces.name: Bạch Hoa
provinces.lore: Coastal forest climbing from the sea into steep hills, its lower slopes a pied grove of white birch and black stumps left by the fire of 548. Its people strip birch bark for writing sheets and boxes and fish the coast. The fire's dead town, Hỏa Tẫn Trấn, still stands burned on the shore.

provinces.name: Thanh Tùng
provinces.lore: River forest in the hills west of the palace, around the memorial pines of Thanh Tùng Thôn. Its people are woodsmen and river folk, many of them children of Hổ Khiếu's survivors. They neither cut nor tap the old pines of the forest above the village.

provinces.name: Tùng Phong
provinces.lore: High river forest in the south of the pine sea, where Vạn Hác Viện's students practise among the villagers. Its people are woodsmen, hunters and zither-string twisters. Striped tigers hold the ridge above, and the wind strings warn the hamlet when the wind turns toward it.

provinces.name: Tuyết Ốc
provinces.lore: River forest on the upper river, where the snow lies so deep that the houses of Tuyết Ốc Thôn are built half under it. Its people trap, fish and dig snow tunnels door to door all winter. Behind the village lies a forest where the drifts are deeper than a man is tall.

provinces.name: Hàn Mai
provinces.lore: Wide river forest around Hàn Mai Thôn and its plum. Its people farm the river flats, fish and gather wild plums from the woods. Since 1105 the swordsmen of Ngạo Tuyết Phái have trained in the plum wood above the village.

provinces.name: Bạch Lang
provinces.lore: River forest around the old den of the white wolf king that Thôi Khinh Hồng slew. Its people hunt, fish and lime the den's boulders white each spring. Grey wolves still prowl a knoll nearby, and the village watches them closely.

provinces.name: Ba Quang
provinces.lore: A strip of forest coast and small stepped lakes below the ridges. Its people fish the lakes and the shore and ferry Cửu Cao's riders over the water. The ruins of an older port lie on the coast to the east, a reminder of why Ba Quang builds well back from the tide line.

provinces.name: Hạc Quy
provinces.lore: Gentle forested river country with marsh meadows where the cranes come down each year. Villagers farm millet and beans and keep the landing pool clear for the birds. A small Wood vein lies in the woods west of the village, and the crane riders rest their mounts on it after long flights.

provinces.name: Lộc Uyển
provinces.lore: High meadows and open forest where the steppe begins, under Thiên Xu's old ban on hunting. Its people keep goats, gather shed antlers and cut hay. On a wooded rise stand the empty halls of Bạch Lộc Quán, the little abbey that first asked the Pivot to protect the deer.

provinces.name: Đỗ Quyên
provinces.lore: Low forest and reed swamp run down to a grey shore of black shingle. The people fish and cut timber and leave the red azalea slopes untouched, because they hold the flowers to be the dead of the old eruption. Băng Tâm takes its tax here in dried fish and fir planks.

provinces.name: Hoàng Oanh
provinces.lore: A sheltered coastal valley of willow and fir, warmer than the land around it, where orioles spend the winter. Its people fish and weave the straw bird shelters, and they sell willow baskets up and down the coast. Nuns of Lê Hoa Am come down in the cold months only to hear the birds.

provinces.name: Ngư Đàm
provinces.lore: Dry steppe around an oasis of fish ponds beside a barren salt sea. Its people raise carp and dates and send live fish to the seat in water jars. An Earth vein lies under the pond fields.

provinces.name: Liên Đường
provinces.lore: A small green hollow of spring-fed grassland on the coast. Its people live on lotus root and seed and on what caravans spend when they stop to look. Dạ Quang's riders water their horses here and leave the flowers alone.

provinces.name: Mã Minh
provinces.lore: Grassland behind the range where herders have run horses since 100. They sell remounts to Băng Tâm's caravans and anyone who pays. The old wells to the west lie under the sand of 1050.

provinces.name: Tiều Lộ
provinces.lore: River forest on the edge of Vô Tung Lâm, running down to the shore. Its woodcutters are the only people who can find the forest paths after a night's snow, and they sell timber and guiding. It answers to Trạc Anh Đài.

provinces.name: Lâm Ẩn
provinces.lore: A small stretch of old fir forest on a quiet inlet. Its people are trackers whom hunters from Mộc Lan hire. The ruin of a trackers' academy lies in the woods.

provinces.name: Lô Hoa
provinces.lore: Forest and reed marsh on the grassy south coast. Its people cut reeds for thatch, mats and quilts and sell the reed-flower down the coast. Blue lynxes hunt in the woods behind.

provinces.name: Bối Sa
provinces.lore: Flat grass and dry steppe running down to a white shell beach. Its fishers and shell-gatherers trade old shell money for small things and new shells to the mainland. A warm pool behind the dunes is where the shell-sorters soak their hands after the cold season's work.

provinces.name: Lãng Thạch
provinces.lore: Grassy shore and bamboo thickets around the split sea stack of Wave Rock. The village answers to Bình Thủy Môn and lives by fishing and by rowing visitors into the sea cave of old Cô Phàm charts. Great claw crabs come up out of the surf onto the grass, and the fishers count them a worse nuisance than storms.

provinces.name: Dương Liễu
provinces.lore: Dunes and coastal grass held in place by long rows of willows, with forest on the higher ground behind. The villagers fish and tend their willow rows, which they began planting after the sands buried Hải Khúc Trấn. Sand pythons lie up in the warm dunes, and children are taught to walk only on the willow paths.

provinces.name: Tình Sa
provinces.lore: A sunny river mouth of grass and bamboo, with the empty quays of Bích Không Cảng on its shore. Its fishers dry their catch on the sandbar beside the driftwood whale. A hot spring inland is where the islanders go to wash after a storm has passed, and they say it always rises clearer when the rain stops.

provinces.name: Nguyệt Loan
provinces.lore: Grass, bamboo and broad-leaf forest round the crescent cove where the island's fleets run from storms. Its people fish, mend boats and keep the storm shed hung with carved moons. Inland under the cassia trees runs a quiet spirit vein that Lạc Hà's disciples visit when they come over to the island.

provinces.name: Điền Viên
provinces.lore: Forest and garden fields on the plain coast where Nhạn Thanh's scholars retire to farm. The village answers to Mục Vân Trang and lives by vegetables, orchards and letters written for herders. A quiet Wood vein under its orchards draws old scholars who have taken up cultivation late.

provinces.name: Yến Quy
provinces.lore: Grass and forest on the plain coast around the old farm where the swallows return each spring. Its farmers plant by the birds. A warm spring in the fields is where the swallows bathe before they nest.

provinces.name: Chu Tân
provinces.lore: Low wet grass and forest on a shore below the level of the high tide, round the old ford whose river has wandered away. The village answers to Mục Vân Trang and hauls travellers and herds across the tidal creek. A warm pool by the old ford is where the ferrymen thaw out after winter crossings.

provinces.name: Lô Cảng
provinces.lore: Grass and forest around the reed harbour where Lạc Hà keeps its western watch. Watchmen and fishers share the land and the tower lights a fire at strange sails. A hot spring inland warms the watchmen after their nights on the tower.

provinces.name: Diêm Điền
provinces.lore: Flat grass and forest along a coast of glittering salt pans, the oldest on the continent. Its people rake salt and sell it up and down the plain. On the shore lie the drowned walls of Triều Một Trấn, a town the sea took.

provinces.name: Mộc Hương
provinces.lore: River forest and steppe on the northern edge of the plain, grown with scented incense trees. Its woodcutters cut only fallen and dying trees for the Pivot Hall's fires. Spirit horses run wild on the steppe beyond the groves, and the villagers keep well away from their herd.

provinces.name: Thụ Âm
provinces.lore: Dry steppe with a little forest and badland along a river, around the great tree of Thụ Âm Thôn. Its people keep goats and grow millet on the river flats. The roots of the great tree are said to reach down to an Earth and Wood vein under the steppe.

provinces.name: Đào Khê
provinces.lore: Rolling grass and wild peach below the northern ridges, watered by the brook that runs past the old palace platform of Cửu Thiều Cung. Its farmers grow peaches, millet and a little rice, and make peach wine they will not sing over. Phượng Minh sends a disciple each spring to sweep the platform, and nobody asks why the palace bothers.

provinces.name: Hà Loan
provinces.lore: A wide floodplain of grass and reeds where the river loops to the gulf, flooded every autumn. Its stilt villages grow rice in the drained season and trade from boats in the wet one. Phượng Minh's bird keepers have lately settled in the jungle edge above the floods.

provinces.name: Bích Lãng
provinces.lore: A low coast of bamboo groves sinking below the level of the gulf, held back by basket walls of stone. Its people fish and cut bamboo for Trúc Thực Viên, which keeps the coast. Up the river, the empty halls of a Cửu Thiều flute school still stand in the bamboo.

provinces.name: Thủy Điền
provinces.lore: The oldest rice country of the plain, flooded paddies and dry steppe along a river under the western hills. Its farmers have planted here since 140 and still set the plain's first seedling each spring. A spirit vein runs under the dry ground beyond the paddies.

provinces.name: Âu Lộ
provinces.lore: A low marsh coast and oak woods on the eastern gulf, loud with nesting birds. Its people fish from the shore; their forebears were the pearl divers of Châu Lệ Cảng and never dived again. A water vein lies in the woods behind the marsh.

provinces.name: Ngân Hạnh
provinces.lore: Grass and oak woods on a river at the western edge of the plain, rising to the hills. Its people farm rice and roast ginkgo nuts for the road. In the woods toward the hills stand the walls of a music town that emptied when Cửu Thiều fell.

provinces.name: Lý Hoa
provinces.lore: A broad sandy coast of grass and steppe on the eastern gulf, with the burned pearl harbour of Châu Lệ Cảng on its shore. Its people fish and grow white plums. Since the pirate years a hall of watchers has kept the coast, and its lantern still burns over the old oyster beds.

provinces.name: Hoàng Ngưu
provinces.lore: Open grass and steppe on the gulf where yellow oxen graze in loose herds. Its herders breed the oxen that plough the plain and pull its barges. A warm spring in the steppe is where the oxen are washed before the spring blessing.

provinces.name: Kiều Bạn
provinces.lore: Grassy river country with stands of bamboo, crossed by the forest road at the roofed bridge of Kiều Bạn. Farmers grow rice and sugar cane on the bottoms and cut bamboo on the low hills, and the inns at the bridge buy whatever they bring. It is the first stop on the road from the west, and the Tower keeps a toll clerk at the bridge's southern end.

provinces.name: Bình Độ
provinces.lore: Rolling grass and rain forest along a slow, wide river, with bamboo on the higher ground. Villagers farm rice and longans and run the calm ferry at Bình Độ, which carries most of the traffic between Thu Trì and the inland towns. Drums are forbidden on the riverbank for a day's walk either side of the ferry.

provinces.name: Hoa Điền
provinces.lore: Low flower meadows and forest between the river and the sea, kept in long strips of colour for the bees. Its honey, wax and flower oils go down to Thu Trì Thành, and buyers for the Night Rain Market pay well for the honey of the poison flowers at the forest edge. A warm spring in the jungle behind the fields is the province's other wealth.

provinces.name: Yên Kiều
provinces.lore: Damp jungle and meadow along a misty river, held by Hồng Đậu Trang as the approach to its manor. Its villagers fish, grow taro and chew the areca nut of the groves around them, and they work for the manor as boatmen and guides. Guests of the manor cross the misty bridge here, and the villagers say not all of them are counted coming back.

provinces.name: Ương Ca
provinces.lore: Wooded hills and bamboo above a river, terraced for rice wherever the slope allows. Its farmers sing the oldest planting song in the south, and sing it louder each spring to drown the autumn singing from the graves of Lôi Trạch. A grove of lightning-struck paulownia above the terraces supplies the zither makers of Không Mông.

provinces.name: Song Khê
provinces.lore: Low bamboo country and grass between two brooks, west of the old Lôi Trạch marsh. Villagers cut bamboo, grow rice and keep the joined dippers at the meeting of the brooks, where couples come from as far as Thu Trì. Hornets as long as a thumb nest in the bamboo, and the ruin of a drummers' hall stands empty on the grass.

provinces.name: Thượng Độ
provinces.lore: Bamboo and jungle along the upper river, where the ferry rope crosses between its carved stone posts. Its people raft bamboo downstream and keep the charred post that shows how near Phượng Minh's raiders came to the Tower's heart. A grove of purple bamboo above the ferry is cut for flutes.

provinces.name: Hà Châu
provinces.lore: Grass, bamboo and jungle on both banks of a broad river, with the raw new isle in midstream that Thính Vũ and Xuyên Lâm both claim. Villagers fish, grow rice and row out each morning to see whose flag has moved. Lightning-blackened ebony trees stand alone in the meadows, and no one will cut them.

provinces.name: Cúc Viên
provinces.lore: Flat steppe and grass on the northern coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, around the flower village that hid Phượng Minh's scouts in 586. Its people grow chrysanthemums for the palace's autumn rites and fish the shore. A warm spring at the village edge is banked with flowers.

provinces.name: Tang Âm
provinces.lore: Grass and low hills on the coast road where the silk caravans rest under the great mulberry. Its people keep inns, fodder yards and stables. A wood vein runs under the caravan yard, and carters say it is why the tree never ages.

provinces.name: Hồ Tâm
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo behind the coastal dunes, around the round lake that breathes with the tide. Its people fish the lake and the sea. Giant crabs crowd the dune shore, and the villagers trap them for the markets.

provinces.name: Lô Châu
provinces.lore: Jungle, hills and reed marsh on a river in the west of Đan Huyệt Châu. Its people cut reed and have done so since before the pirates came. A forest of water pines grows along the river above the village.

provinces.name: Yên Ba
provinces.lore: The broad forested lowland around Yên Ba Thành, cut by a river, limestone knolls and patches of marsh, is the most crowded land on the cape. Timber, grain, fish and the trade of every cape village pass through its port. Thúy Vi's formation keeps the sea fog off the upper town but not off the woods, where the haze lies green all morning.

provinces.name: Hàn Tân
provinces.lore: River forest, marsh and tundra edge around the ford and port of Hàn Tân Thành. Fishers and ferrymen live by the river and the cold sea, and fir timber goes out by boat. On the marsh coast lie the drowned quays of a town emptied under Tùng Đào's resin tax.

provinces.name: Tùng Gian
provinces.lore: The small river mouth around Tùng Gian Thành, Tùng Đào's first city and port. Its land is all city, harbour and pine grove, with a clear spring running over the stones by the river. Timber, resin and pilgrims pass through its moon gate.

provinces.name: Đào Thanh
provinces.lore: River land and steep forest around Đào Thanh Thành, the busiest city on the river. Timber merchants, river traders and the families of Tùng Đào's outer disciples live here. A spirit vein above the city hums with the pine waves.

provinces.name: Khai Dương
provinces.lore: The forest country around the port of Khai Dương Thành, cut by a river that reaches the sea under the city walls. Farms and timber lots feed the city, and its quays ship timber, furs and Dao Quang iron along the northern coast. The woods inland are kept for the city's shipwrights and its morning fires.

provinces.name: Trường Vân
provinces.lore: Steppe and grassland around the river mouth where Trường Vân Thành stands, Băng Tâm's door to the sea since 470. Caravan guards, chandlers and the sect's officers fill it, and goods pass from camel to ship under the long gallery. Its guard families have never forgiven Hạng Dạ Bôi, who was born among them.

provinces.name: Liên Giang
provinces.lore: Forest around the cold river mouth where Hàn Giang Môn built Liên Giang Thành in 350. Its people fish and pay their tax in ice-fish, as they have since the frost coast fell in 498. A new school of ice-hole cultivators keeps Hàn Giang's old practice alive under Băng Tâm's licence.

provinces.name: Đàm Ảnh
provinces.lore: The broad grass and bamboo country around Đàm Ảnh Thành, the island's old Cô Phàm city on its river mouth. It lives by fish, trade and the painters who come to paint the sky upside down in the pool. A Water vein lies under the land nearby, and some say it is why the pool never ripples.

provinces.name: Nhạn Thanh
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass around Nhạn Thanh Thành, the wool market of the western plain, where a river meets the sea. Its herders drive their flocks to the city, and its lake is where the wild geese come down each autumn. On the steppe shore stands Nhạn Trận Môn, the gate that drills the plain's levies.

provinces.name: Lai Nghi
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass around Phượng Minh's port city at the river mouth, with the broken walls of Vân Môn Thành upriver. Its people farm, herd and work the gulf trade. A fire vein under the steppe is said to stir when the nine tiers play at dawn.

provinces.name: Thu Trì
provinces.lore: The rich coastal lowland around Thu Trì Thành, where the river meets the sea below wooded hills: rice paddies, fish ponds and jungle on the slopes. Night rain on the hills fills the city's pools and the fields together, and the province lives on the port and the Night Rain Market. It is the Tower's richest holding, and its most watched.

provinces.name: Không Mông
provinces.lore: The valley mouth around Không Mông Thành: rice meadows, bamboo and broadleaf woods on the hills, nearly always under fine rain. Many of its families descend from the people of Lôi Trạch and still beat the thunder-day drums each spring. A drizzle-fed spirit spring above the city is shared by the Tower's resident disciples and the city's painters.

provinces.name: Ngũ Thải
provinces.lore: Grass, jungle and bamboo at the river mouth around the five-coloured port city. Its people glaze tile, fish and trade along the coast. A fire vein near the city is where Hùng Phần Vũ is said to have first sat as a boy.

provinces.name: Lam Yên
provinces.lore: Forested foothills climbing to high ground below Thúy Vi Tông, inland and nearly always in haze. Carters, stallholders and herb growers live along the stair road of Lam Yên Thị. A wood spring below the market feeds the herb plots of the lower slopes.

provinces.name: Tùng Hạ
provinces.lore: Wide pine sea along the road to the palace, with Tùng Hạ Thị's ring market at its heart. Caravans, woodcutters and pilgrims fill its roads, and wolves follow the caravans in hard winters. Since 1191 the new Tuần Tùng Đường keeps the road watch from the hills above the market.

provinces.name: Đào Sa
provinces.lore: Sand flats, bog and forest at the river mouth, around the stilt market of Đào Sa Thị. Its people wash gold, fish and work the landing. A poplar wood holds the dunes behind the flats.

provinces.name: Tống Khách
provinces.lore: Forest and low mountains around the market where travellers leaving the frost coast are seen off. Its people sell furs, dried fish and warm wine for the road. The sword sage Tư Không Hạc Niên has lived here since 1130 and teaches no one.

provinces.name: Tương Phùng
provinces.lore: Grass and dry steppe along the quay where the floating market of Tương Phùng Thị rides the tide. Its people are boatmen, stall-keepers and brokers who never know who the next ferry will bring. On the point beyond the market stands the empty hall of a school of wanderers that ended without an heir.

provinces.name: Thiên Quyền
provinces.lore: Mountain flanks and grassy steppe at the foot of Thiên Xu Tông's seat, around the market of Thiên Quyền Thị. Traders, weighers and carters live by the market, and a copper mine above it supplies the bronze for the market's weights. Every road to the seat passes through here, and every load is weighed.

provinces.name: Thiều Âm
provinces.lore: A narrow river valley of bamboo at the foot of Phượng Minh's ridges, with bare rock rising steeply behind it. Its people make and sell instruments at Thiều Âm Thị and hire out as players for rites across the south. Since 1195 the palace has watched the market's musicians more closely than its traders.

provinces.name: Hạnh Hoa
provinces.lore: Mountain and dry steppe along the river below the Tower's southern road, with apricot orchards on the bank and bare rock above. The market at Hạnh Hoa Thị sells the flowers, felt and ore of the uplands, and the sick come to wait for the healer Giả Hồi Xuân. A tin mine and an old stockade of Khải Lôi's time stand in the hills over the road.

provinces.name: Quy Điểu
provinces.lore: Low pine forest running down to the shore around Quy Điểu Trấn, loud with birds every autumn. Townsfolk and woodsmen live by the pearl market, fowling and timber. The winter ice market draws pearl buyers from all three of Tùng Đào's lands.

provinces.name: Mục Ca
provinces.lore: Wooded hills and open grass run down to the sea around the sheepfolds of Mục Ca Thành. Herders and their flocks own the grass; the woods give firewood and a small spirit vein that Thúy Vi keeps for its disciples. On a hill west of the city stand the broken halls of a flute sect that once sang with the herders.

provinces.name: Bạch Sa
provinces.lore: A coastal strip of firs and grass behind the white beach of Bạch Sa Trấn. The Thẩm clan rules the town and the fishing, and its woodcutters supply the net frames and boats. Since 1120 strangers come through asking about tides and streams, and the woods behind the beach are where they ask.

provinces.name: Bách Diệp
provinces.lore: River-mouth forest and steep mountain around the cypress grid of Bách Diệp Trấn. The town lives by cypress resin and incense and the coast trade. A squared summit above the town is said to have been the students' model for the grid.

provinces.name: Tiều Ca
provinces.lore: Forested ridges, limestone gorges and a small volcanic shoulder on the south coast, below Không Sơn's boundary stones. Woodcutters send timber down the flume of Tiều Ca Trấn, and miners dig alum from the volcanic rock. Their songs echo back from the gorge, but only below the stones.

provinces.name: Lộc Minh
provinces.lore: Low river forest and coast around Lộc Minh Trấn, the carvers' town held by Lãng Đào Môn. Its people carve, ferry and fish. Deep in its pines lie the clawed walls of Hổ Khiếu Trấn, and giant otters hold the river bend below the town.

provinces.name: Cổ Độ
provinces.lore: Hill forest and bamboo along the southern river around Cổ Độ Thành and its ferry stair. Its people ferry, smith and drag the old chain links of Thiết Tỏa Quan from the river. A bamboo spirit vein lies in the hills, and an older iron town stands empty upslope.

provinces.name: Hà Bạn
provinces.lore: River forest around Hà Bạn Trấn and its herb mills, which answer to Thải Chi Cốc. Its people fish, grind herbs and ship them downriver. Upslope lie the silted streets of Cựu Hà Trấn, left dry when the river changed course.

provinces.name: Lâm Hạ
provinces.lore: Shaded beech and pine forest around the granary town of Lâm Hạ Trấn. Its people are granary-keepers, coopers and rat-catchers. The giant rats of a knoll nearby are the reason the granaries stand on stone staddles.

provinces.name: Bích Khê
provinces.lore: Forested hills around the green brook of Bích Khê Trấn, with a few steppe clearings on the high ground. Jade-pickers and carvers live by the brook, woodcutters by the hills. Downstream the brook runs through a stand of water firs that the town forbids anyone to fell.

provinces.name: Thanh Bách
provinces.lore: Rolling forest and steppe on the northern road around Thanh Bách Thành. Its farms grow wheat and millet on the clearings, and ore carts from the southern mountains roll through it to the coast. The old cypress wood north of the city gives the city its name and its coffins.

provinces.name: Hòe Âm
provinces.lore: River forest between the sea and the ice mountains, crossed by the old locust avenue that carries the hermitage's supplies uphill. Hunters, fishers and carters live here and answer to Lê Hoa Am. Every hunter still looks for the sealed cave with the sword's cold light that a man of the town found in 930 and lost again.

provinces.name: Hồi Lan
provinces.lore: Steppe running to the desert coast behind the hooked breakwater of Hồi Lan Thành. Southern ships trade here for wool, salt and northern furs. A warm spring in the steppe is where the merchants bathe off the road dust.

provinces.name: Mộc Lan
provinces.lore: Flat forest on the frost coast around Mộc Lan Thành, Băng Tâm's younger port. Its people trade furs, timber and live beasts from Vô Tung Lâm. The fallen gate of Hàn Giang Môn lies in the snow nearby.

provinces.name: Kê Minh
provinces.lore: Grassy steppe and forest on the frost coast around Kê Minh Trấn. Its fishers set out at the first cockcrow and its herders graze sheep on the grass. A dew-fed Wood vein lies inland.

provinces.name: Xích Ngạn
provinces.lore: Red cliffs and rolling grass on the island's high coast, the land of the rust-red sails. Its people quarry and grind the red rock for pigment and fish from the cove below the cliff stair. On the headland stands the ruin of the hall where Cô Phàm's watchers once waited for the fleet.

provinces.name: Hải Yến
provinces.lore: Flat grass coast with patches of jungle, where the sea swallows nest under the town's double eaves. Families here own eaves the way others own fields and sell the nests to alchemists. In the jungle behind the town a Wood vein runs under the shade where the swallows hunt insects at dusk.

provinces.name: Triều Âm
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass around Lạc Hà Tông's own walled harbour at the river mouth, where the bored breakwater sings with the tide. Its people are sailors, customs men and fishers, and Lạc Hà's ships call here first. Crocodiles bask on the shoals upriver, and the city's boatmen keep to the far bank.

provinces.name: Thanh Điền
provinces.lore: Forest and fields so wide around Thanh Điền Trấn that its farmers ride to work. The town answers to Mục Vân Trang and holds a horse fair on the night its head was born. On the coast lie the ruins of Di Hà Trấn, a river town whose river left it.

provinces.name: Thảo Đường
provinces.lore: Farms, fish ponds and forest round Thảo Đường Thành, the granary of the western plain. Its people grow rice and hemp and raise fish and ducks in the grass-banked ponds. On the coast lies Dã Độ Trấn, the older ferry town that emptied when the city was built.

provinces.name: Ngư Lương
provinces.lore: Forest and grass where a plain river spills into the sea through the great zigzag weir. Its families keep the fish of their own stretch of weir. Upstream a white elm wood gives the timber for the weir's frames.

provinces.name: Thạch Kiều
provinces.lore: Rolling steppe and desert edge on a river, around Thạch Kiều Thành, the first city of the heart. Caravans from four coasts meet here, and the farms on the river flats feed the city. Out on the desert edge lie the buried halls of Minh Sa Các, a small sect the sand took back.

provinces.name: Mạch Điền
provinces.lore: Flat wheat and pasture where a river meets the gulf, with dry steppe inland and a fringe of jungle on the shore. Its wheat has fed Phượng Minh's palace since 530. Farmers soak their aching backs in a warm spring by the sea after harvest.

provinces.name: Thanh Khê
provinces.lore: Bamboo hills falling to the gulf around Phượng Minh's port city, with a clear brook running through them to the harbour. Its people build boats, cut bamboo and work the ships of the coast. Above the city lies an empty town the fever took in 812, and the harbour of healing still remembers it.

provinces.name: Hoàng Vân
provinces.lore: Rice land and oak forest on the river where the plain lies flattest, around Phượng Minh's granary city. Its farmers bring their harvest to the round granaries by barge. Spirit boars come out of the forest at harvest, and the granary keepers pay hunters to meet them.

provinces.name: Đạo Hương
provinces.lore: Rice fields and woods running from a river to the gulf, with steep hills behind. The Vương family has planted a new field here every generation since 520. A clear lake in the woods reflects the hills so exactly that the Vương paint it on their betrothal letters.

provinces.name: Lục Dã
provinces.lore: Green meadows and steppe on the gulf with hills to the west, given to Lễ Tuyền Phái for its herb gardens in 662. Its people grow and dry healing herbs. A millstone town in the hills above was buried by a landslide in 1062.

provinces.name: Bình Dã
provinces.lore: An open plain cleared from the forest, ringed by bamboo and broadleaf woods, where rain comes less often than anywhere else in the south. Forest folk bring their wet harvests to dry on the great yard of Bình Dã Trấn, and the plain grows sesame and millet that would rot elsewhere. In the bamboo south of the town stand the empty halls of a school that left when the Tower opened its doors to the ma đạo.

provinces.name: Xuân Thảo
provinces.lore: A small, rich stretch of river meadow, bamboo and jungle around Xuân Thảo Thành, on the forest half of the Petal Shore that the Pivot gave the Tower. The burned orchards are long grown over, and peaches still fruit here and there among the banana trees. Farmers plant a peach stone at the corner of every new field for luck.

provinces.name: Lãng Hoa
provinces.lore: Grass and wind-bitten steppe on the coast around Lãng Hoa Thành, at the mouth of a river. Its fishers and salt-boilers came down to the shore after the Pirate Purge, and its children still race the spray along the sea wall. A spirit eye of sea air on the steppe behind the city is the province's one cultivation ground.

provinces.name: Vọng Hải
provinces.lore: Coastal bamboo and grass at a river mouth below low sea cliffs, held by Xuyên Lâm Môn. Its people fish, cut bamboo and keep the cliff watchtowers manned, though no pirate has come in centuries. Armoured scale-beasts dig their burrows in the bamboo behind the town.

provinces.name: Phong Đăng
provinces.lore: Fertile river meadows, bamboo and jungle on the coast, the best grain land of the Tower's south. The Lục family's carts are weighed first on the great steelyard each year, and the Tower collects its grain tax here before anywhere else. Thunder bamboo grows in the groves, and in the hills above, a small school calls the rain for the harvest.

provinces.name: Thạch Cơ
provinces.lore: Flat grass and steppe on the northern gulf around the port that grew from the fleet's jetty. Its people work the ships and the shipyard. An earth vein under the shore is said to be why the jetty stood for four centuries before the storm.

provinces.name: Tang Điền
provinces.lore: Red-soiled grass and steppe on the coast, planted in mulberry since 200. Its people raise silkworms and reel silk, and the town belongs to Phần Vũ Đường. A vein runs under the red earth, and the silk women say it is what puts fire in the thread.

provinces.name: Tuyết Lộc
provinces.lore: A cold strip of forest, lichen tundra and frozen bog on the snowy north shore, grazed by the reindeer of Tuyết Lộc Thôn. Herders trade hides and antler for salt with the Băng Tâm fishers who share this shore since the Long Lake War. Snow leopards still come down from the bogs in hard winters.

provinces.name: Hàn Yên
provinces.lore: A small stretch of pine and birch on the shore around Hàn Yên Thôn, where winter smoke hangs frozen over the chimneys. Its people fish through the ice and cut firewood. The village bell still calls the children in before dusk, a habit kept since the snow-leopard hunt of 610.

provinces.name: Noãn Ốc
provinces.lore: A sheltered shore of pine around the domed stone houses of Noãn Ốc Thôn and its hot spring. Its people fish and rent bath hours to old cultivators who come to soak their bones each winter. Tùng Đào counts the hamlet among the warmest places of its cold north.

provinces.name: Mạch Lãng
provinces.lore: Wheat on warm volcanic ash, walled in black lava stone, fills the open land between the woods and the sea. The farmers of Mạch Lãng Thôn are the oldest on the cape, and their wheat feeds Mục Ca and Yên Ba. Sea pines grow along the shore where the ash thins to sand.

provinces.name: Phong Phàm
provinces.lore: A small windy headland of grass and wind-bent woods above the boat sheds of Phong Phàm Thôn. Its people are sailors and pilots, hired by merchants up and down the coast. Every tree on the point leans the same way, and the pilots read the wind in them as well as in their streamers.

provinces.name: Phần Vũ
provinces.lore: Grass, jungle and steep volcanic ground on the east coast, where Phần Vũ Đường tempers its disciples in the vents and Chúc Dung Khẩu smokes over the sea. Few farm here; its people serve the hall and its burned. The walls of a fire-silk town that died with Xích Thành stand on the slope.

provinces.name: Phượng Minh
provinces.lore: The high ridges of Thê Ngô Lĩnh, planted with wutong on every terrace, where Phượng Minh Cung stands around its great tree. No farmers live here; the slopes belong to the palace's disciples, gardeners and musicians. Its head Hoa Triêu Dương and first elder Vu Ngô Đồng rule from here, and on a shoulder below the palace the broken fort that held the ridge for Cửu Thiều is left as it fell.

provinces.name: Thải Chi
provinces.lore: Swamp, forest and tundra at the river's northern mouth around Thải Chi Cốc. Its people grow herbs and gather marsh plants, and the valley's orphans learn their letters in the drying sheds. Poison leeches infest the marsh, and gatherers wrap their legs.

provinces.name: Thiên Xu
provinces.lore: The bare mountain of Thiên Xu Tông's seat and its green slopes, the heart of the Bắc Thần Phúc Địa over Tử Vi Mạch. No mortal village stands inside the seat's wards; servants and disciples live on its terraces. Array stone for the sect's formations is quarried just below the halls.

provinces.name: Thính Vũ
provinces.lore: The Tower's own ground: a dormant volcanic cone and the bare high mountains around it, falling through dry steppe to the coast. Banana groves terrace the cone's flanks and the grey lake Tàn Hà Hồ lies at its foot; no village stands within sight of the Tower, and its only people are disciples, servants and the masters who came by night. Rain clouds break on the cone almost every night, so the Tower sits in rain while the steppe below stays dry.

provinces.name: Thu Phần
provinces.lore: Quiet bamboo hills inland from the ruins of Lôi Trạch, covered in old grave mounds and held by Thu Phần Các. Few living people stay here besides the pavilion's disciples; the villagers of Ương Ca keep away, and woodcutters come only by day. Among the graves grows bamboo that sprang from roots the tribulation lightning scorched.

provinces.name: Thúy Vi
provinces.lore: The twin summits of Thúy Vi Tông and the forested mountains around them, with no coast and no river, high and always half in haze. Herb terraces, pill furnaces and the green jade of Bích Ngọc Khoáng are its wealth. Disciples walk the white spiral Haze Walk from dawn to dusk before they take their vows.

provinces.name: Trạc Anh
provinces.lore: River forest on the frost coast around the terrace of Trạc Anh Đài. Fishers and sea hunters live here and swear their oaths only when the stream runs clear. The sect takes timber from the woods for its drying poles.

provinces.name: Trúc Thực
provinces.lore: A low coastal plain of grass and seed bamboo where Trúc Thực Viên grows the phoenix's grain. Its people are spirit farmers and their hired hands, and its seed and beast feed go to keepers across the south. Bamboo rats the size of dogs raid the beds every seeding year.

provinces.name: Tùng Đào
provinces.lore: The palace ridge and the endless pines around it, rising to a thousand metres. Its people are the palace's servants, foresters and the families of outer disciples, and pilgrims climb the ridge only to listen. A spirit vein of wood and water qi below the gallery is where new disciples first learn to hear the pine waves.

provinces.name: Vạn Hác
provinces.lore: Ravine-broken pine forest climbing into high mountain, around Vạn Hác Viện and its pillar pavilion. Zither makers, malachite miners and the academy's students are its people. The rockfall that buried Cầm Tượng Trấn in 1012 still scars one ravine wall.

provinces.name: Vân Khởi
provinces.lore: High mountain shoulders and forest above the south coast, where the abbey of Vân Khởi Quán follows its stream to where the water ends. Hermits, teachers and a few mica diggers live here. Below the abbey stands an empty fort built against Thôn Hải's pirates.

provinces.name: Xuyên Lâm
provinces.lore: A high shoulder of Kinh Trập Sơn above the rain forest, mostly bare mountain with bamboo on its lower slopes, where Xuyên Lâm Môn keeps its gate. Its people are the school's guides and their households, and they live by leading travellers through the forest. Above the gate rises the peak where the school tests its new guides.

provinces.name: Tang Du
provinces.lore: High grass, forest and a strip of steppe on the island's sunset coast, where the last light lies longest. Its few villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below the cliffs. Above the village lie the sand-choked lanes of Hải Khúc Trấn, a town the dunes walked over.

provinces.name: Thanh Đằng
provinces.lore: Deep inland jungle with no river and no coast, hung everywhere with rattan. Its villagers cut and split the canes and weave the baskets and ropes that the coast towns buy. Banyans stand so thick on the high ground that their roots make the paths.

provinces.name: Trầm Hương
provinces.lore: Jungle coast where old agarwood trees grow, the island's richest wood. Its town lives by the resin trade, and its finest kỳ nam wood goes to Lạc Hà's meditation halls as incense. Gatherers who go into the old groves mark their trees with knots of red cord, and stealing a marked tree is the worst crime the town knows.

provinces.name: Xướng Vãn
provinces.lore: Jungle and coastal grass on a low shore of the island's far end. Its fishing boats come in singing at dusk, as boats do all over Lạc Hà's lands, and the village keeps the song even in bad years. Wild plantain groves on the grass behind the beach feed the village through the lean season.

provinces.name: Hồng Thụ
provinces.lore: Jungle running down into a mangrove shore. Its villagers catch crabs, burn mangrove charcoal and gather the island's shellfish. Flying foxes the size of eagles roost in the jungle behind the village and strip its fruit trees at night.

provinces.name: Phương Lân
provinces.lore: Jungle and mangrove on a low shore that dips below the sea. Two fishing clans share the village and have never quarrelled, which the island thinks a wonder. Behind them lies a drowned forest of water pines, cut for boat timber that does not rot.

provinces.name: Nam Minh
provinces.lore: The island's jungle tip, where the mist rises off the deep sea and the mist leopards of Vụ Báo Lâm hunt inland. Its one village fishes the deep water off the point. No one goes inland by the leopards' paths, and Bình Thủy's ferrymen warn travellers away from them.

provinces.name: Ngưu Đẩu
provinces.lore: Rolling inland grass rising to forested heights, the highest farmland on the island. Its villagers raise water buffalo and say their herds were named after the stars over the hills. Spirit porcupines den in the forest above, and their quills are sold to the talisman makers of the mainland.

provinces.name: Mộ Sơn
provinces.lore: Inland hills of grass, bamboo and forest that turn purple at dusk. Its villagers grow tea on the slopes and graze cattle on the tops. A hot spring in the hills is said to make the greedy greedier and the honest clearer, and the villagers drink from it only at weddings.

provinces.name: Vọng Hương
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo along the strait coast beside Bình Thủy's headland. Its fishers dry cuttlefish and sell it to the ferry passengers. Travellers fresh off the crossing wash the road off in its hot spring before they go on.

provinces.name: Lục Trúc
provinces.lore: Inland bamboo forest, with a little grass where the groves thin. Its people cut bamboo for houses, rafts and paper and dig the shoots in spring. Jade-scaled bamboo vipers live in the deepest groves, and cutters wear thick leggings of buffalo hide.

provinces.name: Trúc Phiệt
provinces.lore: Bamboo forest coming down to a sheltered coast. Its villagers build bamboo rafts and fish traps and float cut cane along the shore to the towns. The great grove inland is so old that no one has ever found its far edge on foot.

provinces.name: Lan Chu
provinces.lore: Bamboo and grass on a calm stretch of coast, the island's boatbuilding shore. Its town builds the light fishing boats of Cô Vụ Đảo and is famous for carving an orchid on each prow. Wild buffalo with iron-hard horns graze the grass behind the yards and must be driven off before the timber carts can pass.

provinces.name: Đê Hạ
provinces.lore: Low grass and bamboo on a shore that lies below the sea at high tide, kept dry by an earth dyke. Its people grow rice and raise fish in the ditches behind the dyke. Every year spirit sea turtles come ashore to lay their eggs on the beach outside it, and the villagers keep well clear.

provinces.name: Phong Sào
provinces.lore: Inland jungle with no river and no coast, the island's dark heart. Its villagers climb the tallest trees to take wild honey and wax. A Wood vein runs under the high canopy nearby, and the bees there are said to be larger and calmer than anywhere else.

provinces.name: Thải Noãn
provinces.lore: A forested coast rising to wooded heights, facing the duck-covered isle of Phù Chử Đảo across the water. Its villagers fish and gather wild-duck eggs from the isle each spring, taking care to leave most nests. No sect holds the isle, and the village keeps its custom of waiting for the ducks to part before landing.

provinces.name: Bạch Thảo
provinces.lore: Grass and dry steppe on the coast, rising to bare hills inland. Its herders run sheep on the pale autumn grass and fish the shore. A warm spring in the steppe is where the herds drink in winter.

provinces.name: Thanh Phong
provinces.lore: Wide grass and steppe on a low coast where the sea and the sky meet in one colour. Its town ships wool and hides along the plain coast. A Water vein near the shore is named for the old line about autumn water and the endless sky.

provinces.name: Song Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Dry inland steppe with patches of grass, far from any river or coast. Its herders live by two deep wells and move their flocks between them. An Earth vein under the open steppe draws Mục Vân's riders to cultivate on long journeys.

provinces.name: Vãn Chu
provinces.lore: Grass and steppe on the coast, with a few red badland gullies inland. Its fishers put out in the evening and come home singing in the dark. Black vultures nest on the high ground and follow the herds.

provinces.name: Biệt Ngạn
provinces.lore: Forest, high rock and a smoking volcanic cone at the plain's farthest sea edge, facing the isle of Tịch Chiếu. Its one village of ferrymen rows Lạc Hà's dying elders out to the isle and comes back without them. Out at sea lies Hỏa Ngọc Mạch on Thúy Vi's sealed chart, and the ferrymen do not row there.

provinces.name: Thiên Nhai
provinces.lore: A small high spur of steppe and grass over the sea, the last stop for boats going out to the far west. Its little town sells water, salt fish and rope to the boats. Its people say they live at the edge of the world, and that the sunset is nearer to them than to anyone.

provinces.name: Bình Sa
provinces.lore: Grass and forest rising from level sands to high ground. Its villagers fish and herd on the shore flats. Wild stallions run on the uplands and are the terror of herders and the prize of Mục Vân's horse-breakers.

provinces.name: Hòa Lũng
provinces.lore: Wide coastal grass, mostly ploughed, with a little steppe and forest. Its farmers grow rice and millet on raised ridges against the floods. A Wood vein under the level grass makes the ridges green earlier than anywhere on the plain.

provinces.name: Thán Ổ
provinces.lore: Inland grass and steppe with woods in its hollows. Its villagers burn charcoal in the woods and sell it to the towns. On the steppe stand the empty halls of Phù Dao Quán, a school that ended after the cold year of 1120.

provinces.name: Di Tân
provinces.lore: Grass and forest rising from the coast to high wooded ground. Its town is a crowded harbour for the plain's coast boats. A Wood vein high in the forest draws Lạc Hà disciples, and on the shore lie the ruins of Ngư Hỏa Trấn, broken by the storm of 870.

provinces.name: Mục Địch
provinces.lore: Wide inland grass and steppe, the heart of the open plain. Its herders follow their flocks and call them with bamboo flutes. Grass wolves hunt the flocks in winter, and the herders sleep beside their sheep.

provinces.name: Phùng Nghênh
provinces.lore: Grass and steppe on the coast, with an Earth vein on the rise inland. Its town is known for its inns and its welcome to travellers from a thousand miles away. Herders say no stranger has ever slept outside in Phùng Nghênh.

provinces.name: Sơn Tra
provinces.lore: Forested hills rising to bare mountain on the northern edge of the plain. Its people pick hawthorn berries and make them into sweets and medicine for the markets of Thiên Quyền. A Metal vein on the mountain above draws cultivators of sword arts.

provinces.name: Phong Thực Nguyên
provinces.lore: Steppe and grey badland worn into pillars and hollows by the wind, around the sulphur pans of Lưu Hoàng Khoáng. No one lives here; sulphur workers come in shifts. A Fire vein breathes under the badland floor, and its heat keeps the snow off the pans.

provinces.name: Xích Thổ Nguyên
provinces.lore: Red badlands, steppe and mountain around the cinnabar terraces of Thần Sa Khoáng. Miners and alchemists come and go, but no village stands here. A warm red spring in the steppe is where the miners wash off the cinnabar dust.

provinces.name: Thanh Khoa
provinces.lore: High plain of lakes and a river, between Củng Tinh Quán and the Pivot's mountain, within the edge of the blessed land. Its people grow highland barley and keep yaks along the river. Quartz from its mountain mine goes to the Pivot's formation masters, and the old west fort above the river once guarded the seat's road.

provinces.name: Khung Lư
provinces.lore: Wide steppe and mountain east of the Pivot's seat. Its people are herders who live in felt yurts and move with the grass, wintering by a warm spring in the hills. On a mountain shoulder stand the empty halls of Khuy Thiên Các, star-readers who joined Củng Tinh Quán long ago.

provinces.name: Thiên Lang Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains, forest and high plain on the western edge of Thiên Tuyền, named for the bright Wolf Star that rises over them in winter. No village stands here; gold-washers work its streams in summer. Its pine-shadowed peak is a landmark from the plain.

provinces.name: Thiên Cơ Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Heavenly Pearl Star
provinces.lore: High mountains south of the Pivot's seat, named for the third star of the Dipper. Iron sand is washed from its gullies and carried up to the seat's smithies. Its peak of the nine luminaries is where the Pivot's disciples go to sit alone.

provinces.name: Đẩu Bính Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain, steppe and grassland south of the market, curving like the handle of the Dipper on the map. No one lives here now. A beacon fort on its slopes once passed warnings from the borders to the seat.

provinces.name: Thiên Thị Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short mountain ridge and steppe named for the star enclosure of the Heavenly Market. Caravans cross its saddle on the way between Thiên Quyền and the southern mines. It has no village, only a few herders' shelters.

provinces.name: Ngũ Xa Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains with grassy and steppe valleys, named for the five-chariot constellation. Agate is dug in its rock, and an old stockade where soldiers once farmed lies empty in a grassy valley. Herders summer their flocks here.

provinces.name: Bi Phong Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare mountains and badlands on the western rim of the plain, near the old ramparts of Cố Lũy and the poisoned waste of Chiết Kích Nguyên. No one lives here. The wind moans in its gaps, and herders say it is louder in the year the war began.

provinces.name: Hoàng Bách Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and mountain in the north-west, grown with cork trees whose yellow inner bark is a dye and a medicine. Bark peelers come up in summer and dry their bark on racks. No one stays through the winter.

provinces.name: Tàn Kỳ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain, steppe and badland on the edge of Chiết Kích Nguyên, where the War of Broken Halberds ended in 803. No one lives here; alum is dug by day crews who leave by dusk. Shepherds will not cross its upper slopes, which run down toward the miasma.

provinces.name: Mao Ngưu
provinces.lore: High plain at the western edge of Thiên Tuyền, near the ramparts of Cố Lũy. Its people herd yaks and sheep on the short grass. A hot spring in the hills is where Quý Trường Kích's soldiers washed their armour in the five years they held the ramparts.

provinces.name: Tô Du
provinces.lore: High plain and badland along a river in the south-west of the plain. Its herders make yak butter and cheese and sell them at Thạch Kiều. Lapis is cut in its mountains, and the walls of the old remount fort stand empty on the plain.

provinces.name: Thạch Ốc
provinces.lore: High plain, steppe and badland along a river south of the Pivot's mountain. Its people build their houses of stone against the wind and farm barley and peas on the river flats. A Metal vein on the steppe is said to lie where one of the falling stars of the Wild Age struck.

provinces.name: Ngưu Lan
provinces.lore: Steppe and mountain along a river on the south side of the plain. Its people raise cattle for the caravans and the Pivot's carts. Amethyst is dug in the mountain above, and a Metal vein of high winds sits on a bare steppe shoulder.

provinces.name: Hồ Dương
provinces.lore: Steppe and desert edge along a river, its banks lined with desert poplars. Its people farm the river flats and boil salt from a warm brine spring in the hills. Caravans bound for the desert water here.

provinces.name: Hôi Vụ Hoang
provinces.lore: Mountains and high plain around Chiết Kích Nguyên, the plain poisoned by the battle of 803, and the Vạn Cốt Trủng that rose over the dead. No one lives here, and shepherds will not cross it. Thiên Xu's patrols walk its rim and do not go in.

provinces.name: Thạch Điền
provinces.lore: High plain, forest and badland in the far south-west, more than fourteen hundred metres up. Its people farm small terraced fields walled with stone and keep goats. A sulphur spring and a soapstone pit give them something to sell.

provinces.name: Bách Linh
provinces.lore: Steppe and high plain along a river in the south of Thiên Tuyền, loud with larks in spring. Its people herd sheep and farm the river flats. A Wood vein in a forested fold and a silver sand mine in the mountain lie nearby.

provinces.name: Sơn Dương
provinces.lore: High steppe and mountain on the southern rim, under the hawk cliffs of Thương Ưng Đài. Its herders keep goats on the stony grass. Green jade is cut in the mountain above, and young cultivators climb the hawk cliffs for chicks.

provinces.name: Xuyên Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and steep mountain in the north of the plain, whose peaks stand above the cloud on most mornings. No one lives here; woodcutters from the plain climb up for timber in summer. Its jade hairpin peak can be seen from Mộc Hương Thôn.

provinces.name: Mã Nãi
provinces.lore: Steppe, high plain and badland along a river in the south. Its herders keep horses and brew fermented mare's milk, which they trade at Thạch Kiều. An Earth vein lies under the wide steppe nearby.

provinces.name: Hoang Thành Nguyên
provinces.lore: Steppe, mountain and desert in the south-east of Thiên Tuyền, with no village left. Its name comes from the walls of Lục Hợp Thành on a mountain shelf, a caravan city emptied after the earthquake of 912. Herders pass through in spring and avoid the old streets.

provinces.name: Hoàng Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Desert and dry steppe along a river on the south-eastern edge. No one lives here but a few river fishermen in summer. Golden scorpions as big as dogs hide in its sand, and caravans do not camp in the open.

provinces.name: Du Mục
provinces.lore: Steppe, mountain and high plain in the south of the plain, where herders move with the grass. They winter by a warm spring in the hills. Saltpetre is scraped from a cave in the mountain and sold to Thiên Xu for fire powders.

provinces.name: Liệp Ưng
provinces.lore: Steppe and mountain in the south of the plain. Its people fly hawks and falcons for hares and foxes and sell trained birds at Thạch Kiều. A white-headed peak stands over their village.

provinces.name: Nam Đẩu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the southern rim of Thiên Tuyền, named for the southern constellation that faces the northern Dipper. No one lives here; a few crews dig rubies in summer. Its peak of the longevity star is climbed by old cultivators near the end of their years.

provinces.name: Vọng Dương Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the south-eastern rim, whose seaward side drops to the coast. From its grassy summit the far water can be seen. Azurite is dug in its flanks, and no village stands here.

provinces.name: Tùng Nhân
provinces.lore: Steppe, mountain and forest north of the Pivot's mountain. Its people gather pine nuts from the forests and herd sheep on the steppe. Its lotus-shaped peak is the first thing travellers from the north see of the seat's mountains.

provinces.name: Đương Quy
provinces.lore: Mountain, high plain and forest in the north-west. Its people grow and dig angelica root and other herbs for the alchemists of the plain. Dark ore is dug in the mountain above the village.

provinces.name: Bắc Cực Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains just north of the Pivot's seat, under the pole star in the sky. No one lives here but the seat's watchmen. Gold is dug in a small mine for the sect's own use.

provinces.name: Hoàng Kỳ
provinces.lore: Steppe and forest on the northern edge of the plain. Its people dig milkvetch root on the steppe and sell it to alchemists and physicians. A Wood vein in the forest gives a sweet dew on its leaves at dawn.

provinces.name: Thải Dược
provinces.lore: High forest, mountain and plain in the west, more than fourteen hundred metres up. Its people gather mountain herbs on the forested slopes. A Wood vein high in the forest and a realgar mine in the rock lie above the village.

provinces.name: Mộc Tượng
provinces.lore: Forest, high plain and mountain north-west of the Pivot's mountain. Its people are carpenters who work the mountain timber into beams, carts and array frames for the plain. A warm spring on the mountain is where they rest their aching backs.

provinces.name: Kiều Mạch
provinces.lore: Dry hill grass rising to bare rock in the north of the ridges, with no river to water it. Its few farmers grow buckwheat and graze goats on the high slopes. Phượng Minh's disciples cross it on their way to the northern border.

provinces.name: Thiết Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A wall of high bare mountain on the western edge of the ridges, too steep for fields or villages. Only miners live here, in season, at the black iron workings below the summit. Phượng Minh calls it the western wall of its home and keeps a beacon on it.

provinces.name: Thúy Đồng Câu
provinces.lore: Steep ravines of rock and bamboo east of the palace, planted with wutong by Phượng Minh's gardeners. No one farms here; the palace keeps the slopes for its trees and its fire disciples' training climbs. Its highest peak is said to look like a phoenix's raised wing.

provinces.name: Trúc Ly
provinces.lore: Bamboo hills and a river valley on the south-western slopes of the ridges. Its people weave bamboo fences, baskets and screens and grow vegetables in the valley floor. Their basket weavers make the walls that hold back the sea at Bích Lãng.

provinces.name: Bạch Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High pale crags and pockets of forest in the heart of the ridges, without water or villages. Silver miners come and go from a working on its eastern side. The roosting peak above it is a place of trial for Phượng Minh's wood cultivators.

provinces.name: Cầm Huyền
provinces.lore: Bamboo, grass and forest along a river on the southern slopes, rising to the crags under the palace. Its people raise silkworms and twist zither and pipa strings for the instrument makers of Thiều Âm. High above the village stands the empty hall where Cửu Thiều's chime makers worked.

provinces.name: Trúc Phiệt
provinces.lore: Dense bamboo on a river that runs south from the ridges toward the coast. Its people cut cane and float it downriver in great rafts to Trúc Thực Viên and the coast. A rocky ridge east of the village holds the bamboo ode carved by Phượng Minh's founder.

provinces.name: Thạch Lũy Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Almost all bare high mountain, dropping straight into the gulf on the south-east. No one lives here but copper miners at the sea's edge. Phượng Minh's fire disciples climb its tallest peak to meet the sunrise.

provinces.name: Thanh Trúc Câu
provinces.lore: Rock ridges and bamboo ravines south-east of the palace, wet and steep. It has no village; bamboo cutters and herb gatherers pass through it. Cinnabar streaks the rock of its main peak.

provinces.name: Vân Đào Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bamboo-clad mountains falling to a mangrove shore on the gulf, often lost in sea cloud. No village stands here; azurite miners work a pit by the shore. Fishers of the gulf steer by the cliff above it.

provinces.name: Sa Trúc
provinces.lore: Bamboo and rock running down to a sandy shore south of the ridges. Its people fish with bamboo traps and cut cane on the slopes. On clear evenings the ridge above glows red long after sunset.

provinces.name: Trà Pha
provinces.lore: Grass hills and patches of forest in the north-east, rising to bare rock, without a river. Its people grow tea on the slopes and send it down to Mạch Điền and the plain. A warm pool in the woods above the village is carpeted with fallen wutong leaves every autumn.

provinces.name: Thạch Duẩn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Karst towers, bamboo and rock along the gulf, facing the spotted-bamboo isle of Tương Phi Đảo. No one lives here; alchemists' miners take stalactite from the caves. Boatmen fall silent passing the cliffs, as they do passing the isle.

provinces.name: Lôi Hậu
provinces.lore: A storm coast of bamboo, jungle and rock below the thunder peaks, where Lôi Ngô Lâm takes the lightning. Its people gather the struck wutong for Phượng Minh's workshops, and fish when the sky is clear. The palace has guarded the wood closely since the Thunder Vein War.

provinces.name: Hi Quang Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest mountains of the south, rising to Cao Cương Phong above the coast, with a little volcanic ground. No one lives here; pilgrims and Phượng Minh's disciples climb to the crest at dawn. Realgar is dug on the flank of the old volcanic cone.

provinces.name: Tiêu Giang
provinces.lore: A warm river plain of grass and jungle opening on the southern sea. Its people grow bananas and rice and fish the river mouth. A spirit vein lies in its open fields, and the farmers plant rice around it first.

provinces.name: Bạch Lộ
provinces.lore: Grass shore, jungle and rocky hills along the southern coast. Its people fish the shallows and keep buffalo. Wild elephants come down from the hills to its grass in the dry season.

provinces.name: Hôi Tẫn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High volcanic mountains on the south coast, grey with ash around Niết Hỏa Khẩu. No one lives here; the burned wutong sprout again after every outburst. Phượng Minh's fire disciples come to the vent for trial and leave before dark.

provinces.name: Đằng Khê
provinces.lore: Low jungle and mangrove on a river near the southern sea, some of it below the tide line. Its people cut rattan and camphor and fish the brook. Camphor from its forest goes to Thanh Khê's healers.

provinces.name: Ô Mộc
provinces.lore: Deep jungle on the southern coast, much of it at or below the sea. Its people cut ebony and fish from the mangrove edge. In the jungle stand the burned stockades of a Thôn Hải shore camp, destroyed in the Pirate Purge.

provinces.name: Khổng Tước
provinces.lore: Jungle and rock on a small stretch of southern coast. Its people trap fish and gather the feathers shed by wild peacocks, which they sell to fan makers and talisman makers. Black crocodiles hold the mud shore beyond the village.

provinces.name: Hoang Đằng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and jungle held by the dark apes of Huyền Viên Lâm, too wild for villages. Only miners of red stone come here, and only in the morning. Phượng Minh's disciples hunt the jungle edge for practice, and the apes remember them.

provinces.name: Thạch Lựu
provinces.lore: Upland grass and forest on a river in the north-west of the ridges. Its people grow pomegranates and millet on river terraces. Red sandstone outcrops on the hill above hold a fire vein.

provinces.name: Hải Giác
provinces.lore: A tiny grassy cape at the southern tip of the ridges' coast. Its people fish and gather salt. A spirit vein on the shore rises and falls with the tide.

provinces.name: Đan Kiều
provinces.lore: Dry steppe, red badlands and grass along a river in the north of the ridges, the one dry country of Thê Ngô Lĩnh. Its people graze horses and goats and trade hides at the town by the red bridge. A hot spring in the badlands stains bathers' skin rust-red.

provinces.name: Mục Dương
provinces.lore: Upland grass and forest on a river in the north-western hills. Its people herd sheep and goats and sell wool down the river. Red wolves den in the forest below, and the shepherds keep big dogs.

provinces.name: Ngô Miêu
provinces.lore: Grass, bamboo and forest climbing from a river to the ridges just north of the palace. Its people raise wutong seedlings for the palace terraces, as they have since the founding. A peak above the village is where Phượng Minh's disciples practise their first sword cries.

provinces.name: Minh Tuyền Câu
provinces.lore: A high ravine of rock and forest on the western ridges, cut by a cold mountain stream. No one lives here; the springs whistle through the rocks in the wind. Phượng Minh's elders discourage disciples from lingering to listen.

provinces.name: Thê Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains west of the palace, nearly always in cloud, with forest in the hollows. No villages stand here; miners dig red jade below the summit. The palace gathers fallen feathers on its peak as a rite.

provinces.name: Nhục Quế
provinces.lore: Jungle, bamboo and rock on the eastern slopes of the ridges, wet and without a river. Its people strip cinnamon bark and sell it to the ports. Above them stand the walls of a mountain market town that emptied when Cửu Thiều fell.

provinces.name: Hồng Thổ Hoang
provinces.lore: High mountains and red badlands at the north-western corner of the plain, dry and bare. No one lives here but copper miners in season. Its peak is named for the vermilion bird of the south.

provinces.name: Hoàng Lương
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass on the inland hills west of Lai Nghi, without a river. Its people grow millet and herd goats. Jackal packs den on a rise near the village.

provinces.name: Thủ Mạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains running to the coast at the plain's western border with the heart, where Đan Sơn Mạch lies. No villages stand here; Phượng Minh's guards and cinnabar miners are its only people. The palace has kept the ridge guarded since Thính Vũ Lâu's attack in 1150.

provinces.name: Phong Mật
provinces.lore: Hill meadows and forest above the plain, cool and flowery. Its people keep bees and sell honey and wax to the towns. Golden eagles nest on the cliff above the village.

provinces.name: Tử Thái
provinces.lore: Flat steppe and grass on the southern gulf shore, barely above the sea. Its people gather laver from the rocks and fish the shallows. The burned walls of a salt town stand on the shore, destroyed by Thôn Hải in 764.

provinces.name: Hàm Trạch
provinces.lore: Low steppe and grass on the southern gulf, some of it below the tide. Its people make salt in shallow pans and herd a few cattle. Red ants the size of a hand build mounds on the grass behind the pans.

provinces.name: Thúy Bình Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with forest and bamboo on the western edge of the plain, rising like a screen behind Hoàng Vân. No one lives here; jade miners come up in summer. The plain's farmers read the weather by the cloud on its peak.

provinces.name: Tùng Ngạn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and forest falling to a small stretch of western coast. No village stands here; marble is quarried at the shore. Its peak looks like an ox lying down, and the herders of Hoàng Ngưu bow to it.

provinces.name: Trùng Loan Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Fold after fold of high mountain and forest on the western coast, empty of villages. Woodcutters and herb gatherers work its lower slopes. Its tallest peak carries the sound of Lai Nghi's dawn bells back across the plain.

provinces.name: Nhật Xuất
provinces.lore: Grass and steppe at the far eastern end of the plain, facing the open sea. Its people fish and are the first on the plain to see the sun each morning. A fire vein in the grass is warmest at dawn.

provinces.name: Liệt Nhật Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the western gulf coast, hot and bare on their sunward side. No one lives here. Phượng Minh's fire disciples sit on its peak at noon in summer.

provinces.name: Hải Mục
provinces.lore: Wide grass and steppe on the gulf coast east of Lai Nghi, some of it below the tide. Its people graze cattle on the salt grass and fish the shore. Wild iron-horned buffalo roam the grass inland.

provinces.name: Thâm Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass inland on the eastern plain, without river or coast. Its people live by deep wells and graze sheep and oxen. An earth vein runs under the steppe near the village.

provinces.name: Thú Hải Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and grass on the western gulf coast, overlooking the plain. No village stands here; the broken fort that watched for Thôn Hải's sails sits on its seaward side. Its peak looks down on the rice fields like a bowed head.

provinces.name: Đoạn Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare red ridges and badlands at the northern rim of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, where the rain clouds off the sea tear apart on the crests and drop their water before they cross. No one lives here; iron prospectors come up in the dry months and leave before the storms. Herders call it the place where the rain ends.

provinces.name: Vũ Ảnh Nguyên
provinces.lore: High dry steppe in the rain shadow of the mountains west of the Tower, grass on the flats and grey rock on the ridges. Herders drive goats through it in spring, but it has no village and no water that lasts the summer. An old watch fort of Khải Lôi Môn still stands on a spur over the western pass, and a silver mine works the ridge below it.

provinces.name: Hạn Thạch Hoang
provinces.lore: Red badlands, stony steppe and patches of desert between the mountains, crossed by one thin river that runs only after storms on the peaks. Nothing is farmed here, and travellers go round it. A lone stone pillar on its ridge is the only landmark.

provinces.name: Phong Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and sand at the foot of the western mountains, swept by a hot wind for most of the year. Herders from Thâm Tỉnh graze it in the short wet season and leave before the dust storms. The yellow summit above it is the only landmark for a day's walk.

provinces.name: Xích Nham Hoang
provinces.lore: Red crags and badlands with patches of grass, rising to the forested ridge where the black bears of Hắc Hùng Lĩnh den. Woodcutters and honey hunters come up from the forest in autumn, when the bears go down, and never stay the night. It has no village and no road.

provinces.name: Thảo Lư
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grassland sloping from the Tower's mountains toward the coast, beside the grey lake Tàn Hà Hồ. Its herders keep goats and hill horses and sell felt, milk and dung fuel to the Tower and to Hạnh Hoa Thị. They live close enough to hear the Tower's rain-chains ring in storms.

provinces.name: Chương Thụ
provinces.lore: Mixed country of badlands, grass and broadleaf forest below the western ridges. Its people fell camphor trees and boil the wood in copper stills, and its camphor is sold to every sect that keeps books or robes against insects. A quiet spirit vein in the grass above the village draws a few loose cultivators who rent rooms from the distillers.

provinces.name: Trúc Chỉ
provinces.lore: Broadleaf forest, grass and bamboo on low hills inland, wet nearly every night of the year. Its village makes paper from bamboo pulp, and the oiled-paper awnings of Thu Trì's Night Rain Market come from here. Wild boars raid the pulp pits, and a ruined abbey in the woods is all that is left of a school that lasted eight years.

provinces.name: Mộc Miên
provinces.lore: Grassland and broadleaf forest on rolling hills in the middle of Tiêu Vũ Lâm. Its people grow rice on the bottoms and gather kapok floss from the tall red-flowering trees for quilts and padded jackets. A spring of spirit water above the village brims in the plum-rain season and is nearly dry by autumn.

provinces.name: Vũ Tiền
provinces.lore: Open grassland and bamboo on low hills, with dry steppe at its northern edge toward the Tower. Its tea gardens are picked in the days before the spring rains, and Vũ Tiền tea is drunk in the Tower itself. On the steppe at its edge stand the ruins of the lamp-makers' town that lost its trade when the Tower went dark.

provinces.name: Tượng Lộ
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo hills with patches of jungle in the heart of the forest, crossed by a timber road. Its villagers keep working elephants that haul logs to the rivers, and the elephants are worth more than the houses. A spirit vein in the bamboo above the village is a resting place for the Tower's outer disciples on the road south.

provinces.name: Lãnh Vụ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains and cold broadleaf forest in the far north-east of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, nearly always in cloud. No one lives here; the forest is too steep to cut and the summits too cold to graze. The Tower's disciples climb its highest peak to train in the mist.

provinces.name: Lạc Triều
provinces.lore: Low jungle, grass and mangrove at a river mouth on the south coast. Its villagers net fish and crabs in the tidal channels and dry them on racks above the mud. A wood of great banyans stands just inland, and the village carries its dead there.

provinces.name: Da Âm
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass along the south coast, with a few limestone knolls. Its people grow coconuts and twist coir rope for the ships at Thu Trì. An agarwood forest inland is the province's real treasure, and Hồng Đậu Trang buys its resin by weight in silver.

provinces.name: Lăng Giác
provinces.lore: Dense coastal jungle edged with mangrove in the south-west of Tiêu Vũ Lâm. Its village farms water chestnuts and fish in the brackish ponds behind the shore. Great poison toads breed in the jungle pools, and Hồng Đậu Trang pays the villagers for their skins.

provinces.name: Liệt Địa Hoang
provinces.lore: Cracked red badlands and steppe below the northern mountains, without a tree or a running stream. A hot pool stained red with iron and a malachite mine are the only reasons to come. The miners walk in from Thâm Tỉnh and carry their own water.

provinces.name: Lôi Kích Nhai
provinces.lore: A short range of bare mountains and badland cliffs north of the Tower, where the storms off the sea break first and lightning strikes the same crests night after night. The rock is scarred black along the ridgelines. No one lives here, and herders keep their flocks off the high ground in the storm months.
