provinces.name: Đồng Nham Câu
provinces.lore: Ravines cut through green-stained and red rock in the mountains north-east of the Tower, with a little grass in the bottoms. Prospectors have dug test pits all over it and found the copper too thin to mine. One grey peak stands over the ravines and throws the thunder back.

provinces.name: Mã Lan
provinces.lore: High, dry steppe under the northern mountains, nearly treeless. Its people breed the small, hardy hill horses that carry the Tower's messengers, and winter the herds in stone pens. Grey wolves den in the rocks above and take a foal or two each spring.

provinces.name: Khô Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare mountains and badlands just north of the Tower, where clouds that have already rained on the cone drift over thin and white. It is dry, windy and empty. A twin-horned peak marks its centre.

provinces.name: Lạc Lôi Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and red badlands east of the Tower's cone, with grass in the hollows. Lightning falls here nearly as often as on the thunder peaks to the east, and a copper mine works the red rock. The Tower's smiths come down to the mine in storms to quench their castings in the rain.

provinces.name: Thâm Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and high mountains in the north-west of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, in the rain shadow behind the ridges. Its village lives around one very deep well, keeps goats and a little millet, and sends its young men to the mines in the hills. Jade from the black jade mine above it is carved in Thu Trì.

provinces.name: Tàng Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains at the north-western end of Kinh Trập Sơn, with a little steppe and badland on the lower spurs. Clouds pile into its high valleys and sit there for days. No one lives here; miners dig lodestone on one slope in the dry season.

provinces.name: Tiêu Thổ Hoang
provinces.lore: Badlands and bare mountain on the northern side of the thunder range, the rock blackened and fused in patches by lightning. Nothing grows on the scorched ground, and herders call it the Tower's anvil. Diggers come for the red-veined stone of its one mine.

provinces.name: Lôi Minh Cương
provinces.lore: Mountains and high grassland on the northern ridge of the range, where thunder rolls along the crest for hours after each storm. A silver mine works the lower slope. Herders graze the high grass in the dry season and never sleep on the ridge.

provinces.name: Hoang Thành Nguyên
provinces.lore: Steppe, desert and bare mountain beside the Tower's cone and above Hạnh Hoa Thị, dry in the rain shadow. Ash-grey soil fills its hollows, and in the hills lie the buried walls of a city Khải Lôi Môn lost before the Tower was built. A spirit eye of Earth qi on the steppe is kept by the Tower's outer disciples.

provinces.name: Vũ Thủy Câu
provinces.lore: Steep mountain and steppe cut by ravines that run full after every storm and dry within a day. A river threads the largest of them toward the coast. Goatherds use the ravines in spring, and its one peak is named for the clear days after rain.

provinces.name: Thạch Lũng Nguyên
provinces.lore: Mountain and steppe in equal parts, the steppe ribbed with long ridges of stone like a ploughed field. A river crosses it toward the sea at Lãng Hoa. Herders from the coast graze it, and its peak tells the farmers below when spring has begun.

provinces.name: Thiên Nhận Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A block of sheer mountain rising from near sea level to a high crest. There is no level ground on it to build on, and no one lives here. A soapstone mine at its foot sends its stone down to Lãng Hoa.

provinces.name: Ám Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High, bare mountains in the middle of the range, where storm clouds gather dark on the crest before they break over the south. No one lives here. Miners dig a black ore on its slopes and leave when the clouds sink low.

provinces.name: Khởi Trập Nguyên
provinces.lore: A high mountain upland with grass in its basins, where the tiger-kind beasts of Phục Hổ Cương roam and the first spring thunder is said to wake every creature in the hills. A banded iron mine works the slope near the ridge. The Tower's fort on the highland road has lain in ruins since the beasts took it.

provinces.name: Phích Lịch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and badlands around Kinh Điện Khoáng, where lightning strikes the ore so often that the smiths forge in the storms. Its only people are miners and smiths, who come for the storm season. A peak above the mine draws the lightning down toward the forges.

provinces.name: Miên Trùng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High, nearly bare mountains in the eastern range, where the cave of Tàng Trập Động opens and the sleeping creatures wake at the first spring thunder. Hunters gather at the cave mouth each year on the day of Kinh Trập. Above the cave stand the broken walls of Khải Lôi's old cave watch.

provinces.name: Hôi Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Grey mountains and badlands at the north-western edge of the range, close to the Tower. Its rock is pale and crumbling, and a blue vitriol mine works the foot of the slope. Herders cross it to reach the steppe and do not linger.

provinces.name: Hải Vụ Nhai
provinces.lore: Mountains that drop straight into the sea, wrapped in sea mist most mornings. There is no harbour and no village; fishers below steer by its peak when the mist lifts. A rock crystal mine is cut into the lower cliff.

provinces.name: Kinh Đào Nhai
provinces.lore: Sheer coastal mountain where storm waves boom in the sea caves under the cliffs. No one lives here. Its cape peak is the last land the Lãng Hoa fishers see when they sail east.

provinces.name: Hoa Vũ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains around the rain-flower pebble beds of Vũ Hoa Khoáng. Its only people are the Tower's pickers and guards, who sort the pebbles in the rain. The peak above the mine is named for the sermon under which the flowers are said to have fallen.

provinces.name: Tử Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Steep mountains above the purple-gold seams of Tử Kim Khoáng, where storm clouds glow violet at dusk. Miners work the cliffs and leave when the seams glow. A high peak above the mine gathers the lightning.

provinces.name: Cửu Tiêu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest ground of Kinh Trập Sơn, around the split summit of Liệt Khuyết Phong. Nothing lives on its upper slopes, and storm clouds sit on it most days. The Tower's disciples drill here in thunderstorms, past the ruin of Khải Lôi's storm camp and a fulgurite mine.

provinces.name: Thiểm Điện Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains around the Thunder vein Kinh Lôi Mạch, close to Thiên Xu's border. Lệ Tiêu Hồn keeps the vein, and no one comes here without the Tower's leave. An amethyst mine on the ridge is worked under guard.

provinces.name: Đấu Lạp
provinces.lore: Grassland and bamboo between the mountains and the coast, below the Tower. Its people grow rice and weave conical rain hats of bamboo and palm leaf, sold in every market of the south. A spirit vein in the meadows is kept for the Tower's outer disciples.

provinces.name: Hàm Phong Nguyên
provinces.lore: Mountain, steppe and grass sloping to the coast, swept by a salt wind that stunts every tree. Herders and salt-gatherers pass through, but no one stays. An old fort from the pirate years watches the shore from a spur.

provinces.name: Bạo Vũ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Very high mountains in the eastern range, where storms empty in sudden cloudbursts that send torrents down every gully. No one lives here. The earthquake of 1199 split the stockade on its pass, and it has stood empty since.

provinces.name: Liên Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains whose crests run so close together that the clouds over them join into one roof. Nothing settled lives here. Its tall peak can be seen from Xuyên Lâm Môn's gate.

provinces.name: Vân Thảo Nguyên
provinces.lore: High grassland and mountain on the northern edge of the range, its meadows often under low cloud. Deer graze the high grass, and herders bring cattle up in summer. There is no village, only summer huts of stone.

provinces.name: Chấn Thiên Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains beside Kinh Lôi Mạch, where the thunder is loud enough to shake stones loose. Gold sand washes out of its streams after storms. The ruin of the fort that guarded the vein in the Thunder Vein War stands on its lower ridge.

provinces.name: Lâm Vụ Câu
provinces.lore: Mountain ravines filled with broadleaf forest and mist, cut by a river running south. Charcoal burners and agate diggers work its lower slopes. Its forested peak is green to the top.

provinces.name: Thán Diêu
provinces.lore: Forest, mountain and grass in the hills east of Không Mông, with charcoal kilns smoking in every clearing. The charcoal feeds the smelters of the iron mine above the village. A peak shaped like a cockscomb stands over the kilns.

provinces.name: Thanh Chướng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forested mountains standing in rows like green screens above the bamboo country. No one lives here, but woodcutters climb its lower slopes for hardwood. Rain comes to it every evening.

provinces.name: Xuân Duẩn
provinces.lore: Bamboo forest and grass in the low eastern hills. Its villagers dig bamboo shoots in spring and dry them for the cities, and cut nanmu timber in the forest above. Xuyên Lâm's guides pass through on the forest road.

provinces.name: Dẫn Lộ
provinces.lore: Bamboo forest below the high shoulder where Xuyên Lâm Môn keeps its gate. The households of the school's guides live here, and children learn the forest roads before they can read. The giant centipedes in the bamboo above are the first danger every guide is taught.

provinces.name: Phạt Trúc
provinces.lore: Almost pure bamboo forest on low hills around Đả Diệp Lâm. Its villagers cut and sell bamboo poles but leave alone the clearing of stumps where Xuyên Lâm's disciples train. The rain on the leaves is so loud that in a downpour the villagers talk in hand signs.

provinces.name: Cố Trạch
provinces.lore: Low coastal grass, bamboo and jungle at the river mouth where the ruins of Lôi Trạch Thành stand in the marsh. Eel fishers and reed cutters live here; most of the old city's families moved up the valley to Không Mông long ago. The bamboo inland grows over the graves that Thu Phần Các keeps.

provinces.name: Tử Thái
provinces.lore: Coastal grass and jungle on a sheltered shore. Its villagers farm laver on bamboo frames in the shallows and dry it in purple sheets. A spirit spring in the meadows rises and falls with the tide.

provinces.name: Tiêu Viên
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and bamboo in the low inland hills. Its people grow bananas and plantains and weave mats from the fibre. A lychee grove on the hill above is the pride of the province.

provinces.name: Thiên Mục Nguyên
provinces.lore: High grassland among mountains on the northern rim of the range. Herders bring cattle up in summer and leave before the storm season. A white jade mine works the ridge, and the peak above it glows in storms.

provinces.name: Đạo Hoa
provinces.lore: Low jungle and paddy grass inland from the coast, flat and wet. Its villagers grow two rice harvests a year and fish the paddies. A forest of hanging vines fills the wet ground above the village.

provinces.name: Ôn Sa
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and a small volcanic mountain on the coast. Its beaches are warm underfoot from the fire below, and the villagers fish and gather sulphur. On the volcano's flank lies the sulphur town the mountain buried in 1013.

provinces.name: Phiệt Hộ
provinces.lore: Dense jungle along a river mouth on the south coast. Its people float timber rafts down the river to the sea and sell them at Phong Đăng and Không Mông. Old elephants come out of the jungle to die on a barrow ridge in the grass.

provinces.name: Phù Ốc
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass along a river near the coast, flooded every wet season. Its villagers live in houses built on rafts that rise with the floods. A Wood vein in the jungle above is wrapped in wisteria.

provinces.name: Yên Vũ
provinces.lore: Wide coastal grassland with jungle and bamboo at the eastern end of the Tower's coast. Its town trades fish, grain and bamboo by sea. Wild buffalo roam the grass behind the town, and the herders follow them rather than drive them.

provinces.name: Mãn Võng
provinces.lore: Coastal jungle and grass at the western end of the Kinh Trập shore. Its fishers bring in full nets most days and dry the catch on the beach. Crocodiles lie on the wet flats behind the shore.

provinces.name: Ngư Hỏa
provinces.lore: Jungle down to the shore on the south coast. Its fishers go out at night with torches on their boats, and the lights of the fleet are the brightest thing on the dark coast below the Tower. Bats roost by the thousand in the jungle above the village.

provinces.name: Phong Hỏa Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and steppe at the western end of the range, close to the Tower, with old beacon sites on every spur. A realgar mine works the lower slope. The fort that watched the western road has stood empty since the lightning drove its garrison out.

provinces.name: Tiễu Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A wall of bare mountain in the north of the range, all cliff and scree. No one lives here; miners reach its one mine by rope. Its summit is one of the first to catch the storms.

provinces.name: Trầm Lôi Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A broad mountain mass in the middle of the range, its valleys forested and its crest bare. Thunder here is low and long, more felt than heard. An azurite mine on its flank and a high peak are its only marks.

provinces.name: Phi Bộc Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with a little forest, where storm water pours off the cliffs in falls that blow sideways in the wind. No one lives here. Its tallest peak sends down a dozen falls after every storm.

provinces.name: Bắc Thú Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and high grass on the northern edge of Kinh Trập Sơn, facing the lands of Thiên Xu. The Tower once kept a watch fort here against the Pivot and gave it up at the truce. Herders graze the high grass and keep away from the fort.

provinces.name: Bắc Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat lichen tundra on the far northern shore, frozen most of the year and broken only by stands of stunted larch. No one lives here; reindeer herders cross it in summer and leave before the first snow. White bears den along its shore, and Tùng Đào sends no patrols past the larches.

provinces.name: Hàn Sam Lâm
provinces.lore: Dark fir forest thinning into tundra and bog, with no road and no village. Trappers enter it only in winter, when the bogs freeze and the wolf packs are easier to hear. Its timber is too far from any water to be worth the cutting.

provinces.name: Tùng Chi
provinces.lore: Rolling inland pine forest whose people tap resin from the old trees and boil it into pitch for the lake boats. A quiet spirit vein of wood qi runs under its oldest roots. The empty fur town in its hills is a reminder of what happens when a forest is trapped bare.

provinces.name: Ngư Đăng
provinces.lore: Forest and reed swamp along the shore, its people fishing by lantern light on autumn nights. They sell smoked fish to Quy Điểu Trấn and pay their dues to Tùng Đào in pitch and dried fish. Great owls hunt the swamp edge and the villagers will not go into it after dark.

provinces.name: Tùng Than
provinces.lore: Pine forest running down to a long pale beach at the western end of the region. Its people fish, build small boats and gather pine pitch to caulk them. The forest behind the beach is thick enough that Tùng Đào's surveyors once counted its trees and gave up.

provinces.name: Hồi Lưu
provinces.lore: Low forest where a river turns back on itself before it meets the shore, leaving still backwaters full of eels. Its people set eel traps and strip birch bark. They pay Hàm Nguyệt Trang in smoked eel each autumn.

provinces.name: Thán Diêu
provinces.lore: Unbroken inland forest of larch and pine, smoky with charcoal kilns. Its burners make charcoal from fallen and dead wood only, by Tùng Đào's rule, and sell it to the lake towns for the winter. The kiln smoke can be seen for a day's walk.

provinces.name: Nguyệt Tân
provinces.lore: Forest along the river where it runs down toward the long lake, with a small side lake of its own. Nguyệt Tân Trấn ferries timber, pitch and pearls between the lake and the inland villages. It is the busiest crossing in Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm outside the pearl towns.

provinces.name: Sái Võng
provinces.lore: Wide pine forest and lake shore whose fishers hang their nets to dry on frames along every path. A small cold lake lies inland among the trees. The province sends fish and net cord to Quy Điểu Trấn and to Hàm Nguyệt Trang's pearl beds.

provinces.name: Liệp Hộ
provinces.lore: Higher inland forest of spruce and pine where hunters' families trap marten, fox and deer. A green-canopied spirit vein of wood qi lies under the ridge. Furs from here are sold at the winter ice market of Quy Điểu.

provinces.name: Phóng Phiệt
provinces.lore: Forest on a river near the long lake, where loggers bind dead and windfallen trunks into rafts and float them down. A quiet pool by the river hides its own small pearl bed. Tùng Đào's foresters mark every raft before it leaves.

provinces.name: Bạch Mang Hoang
provinces.lore: Bare tundra on the northern shore, white for nine months of the year. No one lives here; the cold wind off the water keeps even herders away. A spirit vein of water qi lies frozen in a hollow near its middle, and Tùng Đào's cultivators come to it in summer.

provinces.name: Tịch Ba
provinces.lore: Shore forest whose fishers go out when the evening waves calm. Its people fish, cut ice in winter and hunt lynx in the woods behind. On the shore lie the broken walls of Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn, crushed by the ice shove of 1033.

provinces.name: Tạc Băng
provinces.lore: Pine and cedar forest on the shore near Hàn Yên and Noãn Ốc. Its people cut blocks of lake ice in winter and pack them in sawdust to keep fish through the summer. Tùng Đào's stewards buy the ice for the granaries of the north.

provinces.name: Tùng Kiều
provinces.lore: Upland pine forest on a river, crossed by a long bridge of whole pine trunks. Woodsmen and pine-nut gatherers live here, and the wood above the river is a favourite place for listening to the pines. Tùng Đào has let Sương Tùng Các build its pavilion in the higher woods.

provinces.name: Thạch Than
provinces.lore: Inland spruce forest along a stony river. Its people fish the shallows, gather spruce gum and float small loads of wood downstream. The river is too shallow for boats above the village, so goods go on by mule.

provinces.name: Hồ Khẩu
provinces.lore: Forest where a river opens into the long lake, rich with fish and reeds. Hồ Khẩu Thôn lives by fishing and by the boats that pass in and out of the river. Its red pine woods give the best mast timber in the north.

provinces.name: Tùng Tử
provinces.lore: Rolling forest of old pines whose people live by gathering pine nuts each autumn. An ancient spirit vein of wood qi lies under a single huge tree. Pine-nut oil from here is pressed for lamps all over the north.

provinces.name: Sơn Ổ
provinces.lore: The first real hills of the southern forest, climbing above five hundred metres. Villagers gather mushrooms and wild honey in the hollows and keep a few goats. The ruin of Tà Dương Trấn on the slope warns them not to build where the hillside is soft.

provinces.name: Hệ Bì
provinces.lore: Forest on a river at the edge of Phản Cảnh Lâm. Its people are woodcutters and guides who tie bark strips to the trees so the lost can follow the light out of the forest. Tùng Đào's patrols rest here before skirting the forest edge.

provinces.name: Song Thụ
provinces.lore: Deep river forest of mixed pine and birch. Its villagers fish and gather herbs, and tend the overgrown terraces of the fallen Lãnh Hương Viện for the cold-flower incense herbs that still grow there. Tùng Đào took the old academy's disciples in when it fell.

provinces.name: Phong Khẩu
provinces.lore: High forested hills at the region's southern edge, cut by a windy gap where the old post road once ran. Its people keep goats and gather pine nuts, and brown bears hold the crags above. The empty post town on the gap fell out of use when the road moved.

provinces.name: Đống Thổ Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat, frozen tundra on the northern shore, wet in the short summer and iron-hard in winter. No one lives here. A deep vein of water qi lies under the frost, and it never thaws.

provinces.name: Tàn Tuyết Câu
provinces.lore: Tundra and stunted forest in shallow gullies where snow lies until midsummer. No one lives here now, though the stones of the old Bắc Minh Quán still stand on the shore. A cold spring of water qi runs from the gullies.

provinces.name: Thương Mang Nguyên
provinces.lore: Grey tundra and thin larch woods stretching to the northern shore. Only herders in summer cross it. A vein of frost-bound water qi lies under a low rise, and Tùng Đào's disciples come to temper themselves in its cold.

provinces.name: Mục Lộc
provinces.lore: Inland forest giving way to tundra in the north, where reindeer families of the same stock as Tuyết Lộc's herders keep their winter grounds. They trade hides, antler and smoked meat south. The forest is bowed under snow for half the year.

provinces.name: Bắc Ngạn
provinces.lore: A broad forest running up to the cold northern shore. Its people hunt seals on the ice and fish through holes in winter, and cut timber in summer. Giant boars root in the inland woods, and villagers fence their stores against them.

provinces.name: Băng Võng
provinces.lore: Forest, bog and tundra on the northern shore, where fishers set long nets under the ice. Golden eagles nest on a rock table inland and take hares and young deer. Its people pay Tùng Đào in dried fish and eagle feathers.

provinces.name: Ô Nê Trạch
provinces.lore: A cold black-mud marsh on the shore, frozen half the year and stinking in summer. No one lives here; the poison toads of its shoals are reason enough. Alchemists' collectors come for toad venom in late summer.

provinces.name: Tân Sinh
provinces.lore: Steppe and grass on the north coast below the red cliffs of Xích Thành Môn. Its people herd goats and dry fish, and do not graze the cliffs. The village was rebuilt on the ashes of one of the eleven villages Xích Thành burned.

provinces.name: Thạch Tượng
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and red hills on the west coast around the quarry of Đan Thạch. Its people are quarrymen and masons who cut and dress the red stone. The burned walls of Xích Thành's old quarry town stand on the hillside above.

provinces.name: Sái Võng
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass on the southern coast, low and wet. Its people fish with nets and gather agarwood in the forest. Agarwood from here is burned in Phượng Minh's halls.

provinces.name: Hải Sâm
provinces.lore: Deep jungle down to a mangrove shore on the southern coast. Its people dive for sea cucumbers and dry them for the cities. A great python holds the jungle valley behind the village.

provinces.name: Tân Lang
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and mangrove on the south coast. Its people grow areca palms and sell the nuts along the coast road. A wood vein lies in the jungle behind the groves.

provinces.name: Hương Liệu
provinces.lore: Low jungle on the south coast around a small spice market town. Its people gather and trade spices and resin from the jungle. Old banyans crowd the forest behind the town.

provinces.name: Sa Nhân
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass on the southern shore. Its people grow cardamom under the trees. On the shore stand the ruins of a sea hall of Xích Thành Môn, abandoned in 590.

provinces.name: Nam Tân
provinces.lore: A small, steep stretch of jungle and forest on the south-western coast with a good harbour. Its people work the boats that sail to the far south. Kapok trees flower red on the hill behind the town.

provinces.name: Đậu Khấu
provinces.lore: Jungle hills and mangrove on the far southern coast, near Thôn Hải's old islet. Its people grow nutmeg and fish. A spice town on the shore was burned by the pirates in 771.

provinces.name: Bằng Trình
provinces.lore: A small jungle coast in the far south-west facing the southern sea. Its fishers sail further south than any others on the coast. A water vein on the hill looks out toward where the great Bằng is said to fly.

provinces.name: Hồ Tiêu
provinces.lore: Jungle hills on the southern coast. Its people grow pepper vines on the trees and sell the dried berries to the ports. Dragon's blood trees grow on the slope above.

provinces.name: Lô Hội
provinces.lore: Grass, jungle and bamboo on the east coast just south of Phần Vũ Đường. Its people grow aloe and sell the salve to the hall's burned disciples. A fire vein in the grass still holds the warmth of the vents.

provinces.name: Hồng Sa
provinces.lore: A tiny grassy headland on the south coast with beaches of red sand. Its people fish and boil salt. A hot pool by the shore is warmed by the waves breaking over volcanic rock.

provinces.name: Thiên Nhai
provinces.lore: A tiny grassy cape at the south-western end of the coast. Its people run the last harbour before the open sea. Fire lizards hold the cliff beyond the town.

provinces.name: Thuận Phong
provinces.lore: Jungle and a little volcanic ground on the south coast, facing Đồ Nam Đảo, with the red spring Chu Sa Tuyền inland. Its people fish and sail. They are the ones who row out to leave fish in the great Bằng's hollow.

provinces.name: Phù Thạch
provinces.lore: Jungle on the flanks of a coastal volcano in the south. Its people gather pumice and fish. On the slope stand the lava-covered halls of a Xích Thành pavilion, and a vent above them still burns.

provinces.name: Bái Nhật
provinces.lore: Jungle and volcanic ground on the far south-east coast, facing Dục Nhật Đảo and bordering the snake forest of Vạn Xà Lâm. Its people fish and ferry pilgrims to the hermit Mạc Quy Khư. Every morning they bow to the sunrise over the island.

provinces.name: Phá Lãng
provinces.lore: Jungle on the far southern coast, facing the islet of Thôn Hải Môn. Its boatmen row treasure seekers out to dig in the burned hold, and some of them do not row back. Palms line the shore.

provinces.name: Trúc Lâu
provinces.lore: Wide grass and bamboo on the eastern coast. Its people live in raised bamboo houses and grow rice and mulberry. A young hall of fire-silk weavers has risen on the shore, and the elders of Phượng Minh watch it with interest and some unease.

provinces.name: Cam Giá
provinces.lore: Low grass and jungle on the south coast near the river. Its people grow sugarcane and boil it into brown sugar for the cities. A boiling spring in the fields is used to start the cane fires.

provinces.name: Lam Điện
provinces.lore: Grass and jungle on the south coast. Its people grow indigo and dye cloth and silk blue for the coast. A drowned town lies on the shore, lost to a storm tide in 913.

provinces.name: Lệ Chi
provinces.lore: Grass and jungle on the south-eastern coast. Its people grow lychees and send them to the cities by fast boat. A forest of flame trees burns red on the grass every summer.

provinces.name: Long Nhãn
provinces.lore: Jungle with a mangrove shore on the south-eastern coast. Its people grow longans and dry them for the markets. A mangrove town on the shore was burned by Thôn Hải in 767.

provinces.name: Bạch Diêm
provinces.lore: Grass and jungle on the flat eastern coast. Its people make salt in pans and fish the shallows. A water vein lies among the mangrove roots inland.

provinces.name: Huyết Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A block of high red mountain on the west coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, too steep for villages. Only quarrymen and fire cultivators climb it. Its summit is said to be where the five-coloured bird was seen over the vermilion caves.

provinces.name: Thiên Bạch Nguyên
provinces.gloss: Plain Where the Sky Is White
provinces.lore: Flat frozen tundra along the northern sea, where snow and sky meet without a line between them. No one lives here; sealers come in summer and leave before the first snow. Herds of frost elephants cross it each year and leave tusk-scored ice behind.

provinces.name: Bồ Diệp
provinces.lore: Low woods and wide cattail marsh along the cold north shore. Its people weave cattail mats and baskets, fish the shallows and sell both in Yên Ba. Great otters fish the same channels, and the villagers share the catch with them rather than fight.

provinces.name: Thán Diêu
provinces.lore: Deep inland forest, unbroken for days of walking, with no coast and no river. Charcoal burners live in it and send their charcoal to the furnaces of Hồng Lô Cốc. Among the trees lie the burnt ruins of a resin town lost to fire.

provinces.name: Bích Tân
provinces.lore: Forest running down to a sheltered landing on the north coast, where timber is floated out to sea. The town of Bích Tân Trấn lives by timber and the coast trade, and its old firs are the tallest on the cape. Inland stand the empty walls of a town emptied by the coughing sickness of 760.

provinces.name: Phong Mật
provinces.lore: Linden and maple forest on the coast east of Hồng Lô Cốc. Its villagers gather wild honey and wax, and sell the wax to the alchemists for sealing pill jars. Honey bears compete with them for every hive.

provinces.name: Hàn Loan
provinces.lore: Birch forest around a cold, low-lying bay on the western shore of the cape. Fishers and birch-bark weavers live by the water. In winter the bay half freezes and the boats are hauled up into the birches.

provinces.name: Hải Đới
provinces.lore: Elm forest along a coast rich in kelp beds. Its people cut and dry kelp and sell it inland for food and for the alchemists' salt washes. Kelp dries on racks along the shore for most of the summer.

provinces.name: Thái Dược
provinces.lore: Forest rising into steep high ground in the east of the cape, far from the sea. Herb gatherers live here and sell roots and leaves to Hồng Lô Cốc and to Thúy Vi's terraces. Mountain lynxes keep the upper slopes.

provinces.name: Thuyền Ổ
provinces.lore: Old pine forest on a low western coast, where boats are built from its own timber. Most cape fishing boats were laid down here. On the shore stand the burnt halls of a small sect destroyed by Thôn Hải's pirates.

provinces.name: Tùng Nhung
provinces.lore: Rolling inland pine hills, the highest and driest forest of the cape's interior. Its villagers gather pine mushrooms in autumn and dry them for the markets of Yên Ba. Silver martens live in the high woods, and their pelts are the hills' other wealth.

provinces.name: Tất Thụ
provinces.lore: Inland forest with a few marshy hollows, where lacquer trees grow wild among the oaks. Its villagers tap the sap and sell raw lacquer to the craftsmen of Yên Ba. A belt of the forest is so often lost in Thúy Vi's haze that travellers go around it.

provinces.name: Vĩnh Đông Hoang
provinces.lore: Frozen coastal tundra whose ground never thaws more than a hand deep. No one lives here. A spirit vein of black ice lies under the snow, and Thúy Vi's alchemists come for its cold water.

provinces.name: Man Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest and marsh where a river reaches the sea on the cape's eastern shore. Eel fishers live at the river mouth and smoke their catch for Yên Ba. Water vipers fill the marsh, and no one wades in it barefoot.

provinces.name: Thạch Công
provinces.lore: Forested hills climbing into bare mountain in the east of the cape. Stonecutters quarry the grey rock for the walls and quays of Yên Ba. Higher up lies an empty copper town, abandoned when its seams gave out.

provinces.name: Hải Thúy
provinces.lore: Forest along the western coast where the sea runs green over shallow sand. The town of Hải Thúy Trấn trades fish and timber with Mục Ca and the white sands. Its woods are thick with oak and maple that shed every autumn.

provinces.name: Ma Điền
provinces.lore: Inland forest broken by clearings of hemp. Its villagers make rope and sailcloth for the boatwrights and sailors of the coast. In the deep woods the trees are so still that birds seem quiet there.

provinces.name: Phù Kiều
provinces.lore: River forest in the middle of the cape, crossed by its main road at a bridge of boats. Phù Kiều Trấn lives by the road and the river trade. In the woods east of the town stands Vụ Ẩn Môn, a gate sworn to Thúy Vi that guards the cape's roads in mist.

provinces.name: Mẫu Lệ
provinces.lore: Low forest on a western coast of mudflats and oyster beds. Its villagers rake oysters and burn the shells for lime. Sea eagles nest on the cliffs above the beds and take fish from the rakers' baskets.

provinces.name: Hàm Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest on a western coast where fish is salted and dried for the whole cape. Its village lives by the catch and the salt pans. Inland lie the empty halls of a healers' sect that ended without an heir.

provinces.name: Lô Từ
provinces.lore: Forest with a few high ridges along a coast of rocky inlets. Its fishers fish with tame cormorants. Iron boars root in the lowland woods, and the village fences its fields with stone.

provinces.name: Lăng Giác
provinces.lore: Forest and marsh down to the sea west of Yên Ba. Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the marsh ponds and sell them in the city. Old vines hang so thick in its woods that they make walls between the trees.

provinces.name: Trà Viên
provinces.lore: Forested hills rising to bare heights north of Yên Ba, inland and misty. Its villagers grow tea on terraced clearings, and the haze is said to give the leaves their green. Thúy Vi buys the best of the picking for its seat.

provinces.name: Lạc Tuyết Nguyên
provinces.lore: Tundra and scattered forest on the north-west shore, where snow falls on more days than not. No one lives here now. On the coast stand the snowed-in halls of a sword sect older than Thúy Vi's claim on the cape.

provinces.name: Hỏa Tích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short spine of high mountains and volcanic cones on the south coast, snow above and warm rock below. No one lives here, but Thúy Vi's alchemists climb to Tuyết Để Tuyền for its water. Miners cut black glass from the cones.

provinces.name: Sơn Dương
provinces.lore: Forest on a narrow coast below the fire spine, rising steeply to bare rock. Its villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below. Giant scorpions live in the warm cliffs, and the goats know to stay off them.

provinces.name: Viêm Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains and an active cone on the south coast, with forest only at their feet. No one lives here. Lava still flows from a vent near the summit, and Hồng Lô's alchemists come to it for fire they need not carry from the isles.

provinces.name: Lật Thụ
provinces.lore: A small forested coast at the south end of the cape. Its villagers gather chestnuts and fish. Seals haul out on the rocks below the village.

provinces.name: Tận Giác
provinces.lore: The far western tip of the cape: grass, woods and one high hill over the sea. Tận Giác Trấn trades wool, fish and the passage around the point. On the shore are the sanded ruins of the older town the sea took.

provinces.name: Dương Quyển
provinces.lore: A small strip of dry steppe on the western coast. Its people keep sheep in stone folds and sell wool to Tận Giác. It is the driest land on the cape, and its water comes from wells.

provinces.name: Vân Tước
provinces.lore: Grass and a little steppe along the south-western coast. Its village keeps flocks and bees and watches skylarks rise over the grass. A spirit vein of earth qi lies in the grass near the shore.

provinces.name: Tàn Tuyết Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra with fringes of forest along the north coast, where the snow lingers into summer. No one lives here; fire foxes den on its plain of Hỏa Hồ Nguyên. Brave hunters come for their pelts.

provinces.name: Thương Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: Tundra of grey moss and frozen pools on the north coast. No one lives here. Snow owls hunt over it, and on the coast lie the whale-bone halls of a sect of sea hunters.

provinces.name: Hàn Thạch Nguyên
provinces.lore: Stony tundra rising to bare rock in the north-east of the cape. No one lives here. White bears come ashore from the ice in winter and den on its ridges.

provinces.name: Sương Trạch
provinces.lore: Tundra, thin forest and frozen marsh behind the north coast. No one lives here. Ptarmigan flocks winter on it, and their wings sound like thunder when they rise.

provinces.name: Trùng Sương Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains above the coast north of Hồng Lô Cốc, frosted most of the year. No one lives here. A peak of grey iron-bearing rock stands at its heart.

provinces.name: Liệp Hải
provinces.lore: Forest and tundra on the north-west coast, the largest settled land in the cape's north. Its people hunt seals and fish, as sealers have on this coast since the Wild Age. Great elk move through its woods in autumn.

provinces.name: Bạch Mang Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat frozen tundra on the far northern sea, white in every direction. No one lives here. A deep cold spirit vein lies under the ice, and Thúy Vi's alchemists come for its water.

provinces.name: Phiệt Công
provinces.lore: River forest in the north-east, where logs are tied into rafts and floated downstream. Raftsmen and loggers live along the river. Beavers dam the side streams and the raftsmen break the dams each spring.

provinces.name: Tân Cư
provinces.lore: River forest inland of the Cold Ford, settled by fishers who left the coast under Tùng Đào's resin tax. Its people farm, fish the river and remember the tax with jokes. Deep in its woods lies a forest so quiet that it seems Không Sơn's.

provinces.name: Hồ Đào
provinces.lore: Inland forest of walnut and oak in the north of the ridges. Its villagers gather walnuts and press walnut oil for lamps and ink. In early summer white butterflies fill the woods.

provinces.name: Thủy Ma
provinces.lore: River forest in the north-east, where mills grind grain for the north. Its villagers mill, farm and fish the river. In its woods stands Hộ Lâm Đường, whose wardens keep the northern forests for Thúy Vi.

provinces.name: Tạo Chỉ
provinces.lore: River forest and marsh in the north-east, where bark and hemp are beaten into paper. The village's paper goes to Lam Yên Thị for copied scripture. Brown bears fish the river beside the papermakers' vats.

provinces.name: Phục Linh
provinces.lore: Pine forest on the road north from Lam Yên, gently rising toward the mountains. Its villagers dig poria fungus from pine roots for Thúy Vi's furnaces. An old post town on the road stands empty since the road was moved.

provinces.name: Bạch Lạp
provinces.lore: Inland forest of ash trees north of the seat. Its villagers raise wax insects on the ash and scrape white wax for candles and pill coatings. The forest is loud with birds at dawn.

provinces.name: Thạch Than
provinces.lore: River forest in the east, where the river runs wide over stone shallows. Its villagers fish and ford travellers across. A wood vein rises in the forest above the shallows.

provinces.name: Tử Tô
provinces.lore: River forest east of the seat, where perilla and other herbs grow in riverside plots. Its villagers grow herbs for the alchemists. In its woods lie the ruins of a herb academy destroyed by its own pill fire.

provinces.name: Tỏa Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and high mountain west of the seat, where cloud gathers in the valleys and stays. No one lives here but a few hermits. A pale stone pillar of a peak rises from the cloud.

provinces.name: Vô Thụ Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra on the northern coast with only a few stunted trees at its southern edge. No one lives here. Snow hares in their thousands feed the foxes and owls of the north.

provinces.name: Cửu Điệp Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Folded high ridges and forest just east of Thúy Vi Tông's seat. No one lives here but miners and the sect's watchers. An empty fort above the north road dates from the years the Cold Ford was lost.

provinces.name: Kiều Mạch
provinces.lore: A wide forest east of the seat, running to the coast, with clearings of buckwheat. Its villagers farm the clearings and sell flour to Lam Yên. A great tree at the forest's heart holds a wood vein.

provinces.name: Lãm Thúy
provinces.lore: Coastal forest on the eastern shore of the ridges. Lãm Thúy Trấn trades timber, fish and herbs along the coast. Inland stand the burnt halls of a sect whose head died in his tribulation.

provinces.name: Trầm Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountain and forest in the west of the ridges, where clouds sink into the valleys at dusk. No one lives here now. High on a shoulder lie the buried streets of a mountain town lost to an avalanche.

provinces.name: Bích Chướng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Steep high mountains clad in forest on their lower slopes, west of the seat. No one lives here but miners. Blue-green jade is dug below a cliff that cuts the clouds.

provinces.name: Tuyệt Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest bare walls of rock south of the seat, with only a little forest in the clefts. No one lives here. Miners dig cold iron from its flanks for Thúy Vi's furnace fittings.

provinces.name: Lưu Thúy Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and mountain cut by a river running south, its slopes green with moss and fern. A few miners cut inkstone here for the scholars of Lam Yên. A peak holds the cloud on its shoulder most mornings.

provinces.name: Ngọa Ngưu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short ridge of mountain and forest by a river, shaped like an ox lying down. No one lives here. Herdsmen from below say the ridge breathes on cold mornings.

provinces.name: Vô Nhân Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridges Where No One Is Seen
provinces.lore: High mountain above the south coast where Không Sơn Viện stands empty and unlooted. No one lives here, and Thúy Vi keeps it so. A soapstone pit at the foot of the ridge is the only work done in the land.

provinces.name: Thiên Thúy Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest mountains of the ridges, south-east of the seat, falling to the coast through forest. No one lives here. From its sunrise peak one can see both the cape and the eastern sea.

provinces.name: Lẫm Phong Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra and bare high rock on the north coast, swept by wind off the ice. No one lives here. Ice rhinoceroses cross it on the plain of Băng Tê Nguyên.

provinces.name: Tùng Yên
provinces.lore: Forested mountains west of Vân Khởi, inland and steep. Its villagers burn pine for soot and press it into ink for the scholars of three sects. A peak of pines above the village gives the wood.

provinces.name: Hải Đường
provinces.lore: Coastal forest south of the seat with orchards of crabapple. Its villagers fish and sell blossom and fruit in Lam Yên. Giant centipedes live in a damp valley above the orchards.

provinces.name: Đồng Du
provinces.lore: Inland forest of the far south-east, rising to wooded hills. Its villagers press tung oil for boats, paint and lamps. Grey wolves run on the hill ridge above.

provinces.name: Thạch Hôi
provinces.lore: Forest and limestone karst in the south-east. Its villagers burn limestone for lime and sell it to builders along the coast. A gorge so narrow that only a thread of sky shows cuts the karst.

provinces.name: Sương Tùng Nguyên
provinces.lore: Tundra and pine forest on the northern coast. No one lives here. On its shore stand the ruins of a sect that went out on the ice after a mirage.

provinces.name: Hắc Thủy Trạch
provinces.lore: Forest, tundra and black peat marsh in the north. No one lives here. Frost toads sing in the marsh pools all summer.

provinces.name: Hồi Lưu
provinces.lore: Forest, tundra and marsh where a river reaches the north coast. Its villagers fish the river and the backwaters. On the coast stand the snowed-in walls of a temple of snow-sitters.

provinces.name: Đông Hà Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra and thin forest where a river freezes solid down to the sea. No one lives here. Snow roe deer winter along the frozen banks.

provinces.name: Cô Tùng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Tundra, forest and a few high crags on the north-west coast. No one lives here. A pine-spirit vein lies in its forest, and an old abbey ruin stands on the crag.

provinces.name: Việt Quất
provinces.lore: Northern forest with a little tundra at its edges. Its villagers pick lingonberries and trap fur. Its old town stands empty since the river moved.

provinces.name: Hàn Than Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra, bog and thin forest on the northern coast, with cold shoals offshore. No one lives here now. The fallen pavilion of Vọng Triều Các stands on the shore, and a spring of water qi rises in the woods behind.

provinces.name: Tùng Yên
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest in the north of the pine sea, where villagers burn pine to soot for ink. Tùng Yên ink is sold in every sect library of the north. The misty wood beside the village gives the softest soot.

provinces.name: Phạt Mộc
provinces.lore: Pine forest rising from the coastal lowland into hills. Its woodcutters fell only trees marked by Tùng Đào's foresters and send the logs down to Tùng Gian Thành. A spirit vein of spring-green wood qi lies in its hills.

provinces.name: Phong Mật
provinces.lore: Forested hills climbing toward high mountain west of the palace. Its villagers keep bees in log hives and sell pine honey on the palace road. Above them a cloud forest climbs nearly to a thousand metres.

provinces.name: Hương Khuẩn
provinces.lore: Forest and rocky high ground on the western edge of the pine sea. Its people gather and dry fragrant mushrooms that grow on fallen pine. Black leopards den on the crags, and gatherers go out in pairs.

provinces.name: Cát Chi
provinces.lore: Forest rising from low valleys into steep hills. Its people tap pine resin for incense and varnish, under foresters' rules on how many cuts a tree may bear. A heavy vein of earth qi lies under the hill above the village.

provinces.name: Hương Khách
provinces.lore: Hill forest south of the palace ridge, on the pilgrims' road. Its village lives by lodging and feeding pilgrims, who climb on to the ridge to listen to the pines. The wood above the village sounds so like the sea that pilgrims sometimes stop there and go no further.

provinces.name: Tiều Phu
provinces.lore: High forest and rock above the ravines, home to woodsmen who sell firewood and charcoal to Vạn Hác. White apes hold the ridge above a thousand metres. The ginseng town of Thải Tham Trấn was driven out by those apes in 979.

provinces.name: Mục Dương
provinces.lore: High forest climbing to bare rock above a thousand metres. Its shepherds graze goats and sheep in the clearings and on the high meadows. Dwarf pines crouch on the summits where nothing else grows.

provinces.name: Lưu Mộc
provinces.lore: River forest south-east of the palace, its river carrying driftwood down from the mountains. Villagers gather the driftwood and float logs to the lowlands. The red-barked pines above the river are among the oldest in the pine sea.

provinces.name: Trúc Ly
provinces.lore: High forest where the first bamboo of the south creeps in among the pines. Villagers weave bamboo fences, baskets and mats. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under a still grove on the slope.

provinces.name: Liệp Hồ
provinces.lore: Forest, tundra and bog on the northern coast. Its people hunt foxes and trap for furs and fish the coast in summer. Grey wolves hold a knoll inland and take a share of every winter's catch.

provinces.name: Bán Sơn
provinces.lore: Forested mountain climbing to over sixteen hundred metres south-east of the palace. Its village sits halfway up and lives by goats, herbs and the disciples who climb to the peak. The peak's metal qi draws Tùng Đào's disciples in summer.

provinces.name: Vân Ổ
provinces.lore: High mountain and forest on the eastern edge, often sunk in cloud. Its villagers herd goats and gather mountain herbs. A slender jade-grey peak rises above the hollow.

provinces.name: Lạc Thạch
provinces.lore: High forest under crags that shed stones every spring. Villagers quarry the fallen stone and carve millstones. The avalanche that buried Hàn Thạch Trấn in 1151 is still remembered in every house.

provinces.name: Thảo Pha
provinces.lore: Forested hills opening into grassy slopes in the south. Its people graze cattle on the slopes and cut yew in the woods for bows. It is the warmest land in the pine sea.

provinces.name: Thạch Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Forest and high rock in the south-east, its village gathered around a deep stone well. Its people herd goats and dig a little copper from the hill. Giant flying squirrels glide over the crags at dusk.

provinces.name: Hôi Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountain near the border of the heart, rising to over eighteen hundred metres. No one lives here but Tùng Đào's watch on Thương Tùng Mạch and the miners of the grey iron mine. The rock is grey like the pines on the summit.

provinces.name: Tửu Phường
provinces.lore: River forest in the far south, where villagers brew pine-needle wine and sell it on the road to Cổ Độ. Venom hornets nest in the woods behind. The wine is said to taste of the wind in the pines.

provinces.name: Quan Hạ
provinces.lore: High mountain, forest and grassland around the broken walls of Thiết Tỏa Quan. Its village lives by goats and the black iron mine above. Tùng Đào's elders bring disciples here to see what breaking the peace cost.

provinces.name: Thủ Mộ
provinces.lore: Quiet northern forest around the fallen temple of Khô Mộc Tự. Its villagers keep the temple's graves and gather firewood and fungus. The forest beside it is so still that birdsong carries for a mile.

provinces.name: Mộc Nhĩ
provinces.lore: Damp northern forest where wood-ear fungus grows thick on fallen logs. Its people gather and dry it for the markets. The forest is green and misty even in late autumn.

provinces.name: Tùng Hoa
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest that turns the air yellow with pollen each spring. Villagers collect the pollen for cakes and medicine. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under a wave of green hills.

provinces.name: Mộc Tập
provinces.lore: River lowland in the north-east of the pine sea, where the timber of the north is gathered and sold. Mộc Tập Trấn holds a timber fair each spring. Dawn redwoods grow along the river.

provinces.name: Lâu Thuyền
provinces.lore: Coastal forest whose town builds ships from straight pine. Lâu Thuyền Trấn launches Tùng Đào's coastal ships and Lãng Đào's sea-going barges. Its mast pines are guarded by foresters.

provinces.name: Thải Tân
provinces.lore: Inland forest of mixed pine and broadleaf. Its villagers gather firewood and sell it to the coast towns. It is the plainest land in the pine sea, and its people are proud of it.

provinces.name: Triều Thanh
provinces.lore: Coastal forest dipping below the sea in places. Its fishers listen to the tide from their houses. The sea wind bends the pines along the shore.

provinces.name: Sóc Phong Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat tundra on the northern coast, scoured by the north wind. No one lives here. A cold spring of water qi rises in its middle.

provinces.name: Điếu Đài
provinces.lore: River forest near the lower river, its people fishing from stone terraces on the bank. A spirit vein of soft water qi lies near the river. The drowned abbey of Tĩnh Thủy Quán stands in the woods.

provinces.name: Lư Từ
provinces.lore: River forest where villagers fish with trained cormorants. They sell fish at Đào Thanh. The maples behind the village turn red each autumn.

provinces.name: Mộc Tượng
provinces.lore: Inland forest whose villagers are carpenters, building boats and houses for the river towns. Wild oxen graze the clearings. Its carpenters are hired as far as Tùng Gian.

provinces.name: Mạch Hương
provinces.lore: River lowland where villagers grow barley and wheat on the flood flats. Its grain goes to the granaries of Lâm Hạ. An elm wood shelters its fields.

provinces.name: Hoành Độ
provinces.lore: Low river forest at a crossing of the Nine-Bend River. Its people run a ferry and fish. Lãng Đào takes a share of its fares.

provinces.name: Ngưu Lan
provinces.lore: Inland forest and clearings where villagers keep oxen for the river towns' carts. Giant badgers dig their burrows on a knoll nearby. Oxen from here pull the timber to the river.

provinces.name: Hà Đê
provinces.lore: River lowland behind a long earth levee, raised after the flood of 700. Its people farm the flats and mend the levee every spring. A spirit vein of water qi runs beside the river.

provinces.name: Thủy Xa
provinces.lore: River forest where villagers lift water to their fields with tall waterwheels. Its people farm and grind grain. The frost-leaf forest behind turns red early.

provinces.name: Thải Dược
provinces.lore: Inland hill forest where villagers gather wild herbs for Thải Chi Cốc. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under the hill. Herb gatherers come from all over the basin.

provinces.name: Thạch Lũy
provinces.lore: Inland forest and hills where villagers build stone walls around their fields. Its people farm and gather firewood. A grey cypress wood climbs the hill.

provinces.name: Hoang Tự Câu
provinces.lore: Forest and tundra in the north, with gullies where a temple stood before Tùng Đào came. No one lives here now. A northern birch wood shelters the ruins.

provinces.name: Tân Lưu
provinces.lore: River forest on the new course of the river, near the dry bed of Đông Lưu Thành. Tân Lưu Trấn grew on the new current, and its people fish, farm and trade. Children dig for coins on the old bed since the flood of 1198.

provinces.name: Độc Mộc
provinces.lore: River forest whose villagers cross the river on a single great log. Its people fish and carve dugout canoes. Ospreys nest on a rock above the river.

provinces.name: Sài Môn
provinces.lore: Hill forest where villagers live quietly behind brushwood gates. Its people gather firewood and pine nuts. A cloud pine forest climbs the hill.

provinces.name: Tùng Lộ
provinces.lore: Inland hill forest where villagers dig pine truffles with trained pigs. The truffles sell well in Đào Thanh. A forest of tall pines like a thousand pillars rises behind.

provinces.name: Cung Tiễn
provinces.lore: Hill forest where villagers make bows and arrows for hunters and Tùng Đào's guards. Its people hunt and craft. Sacred old trees stand on the hill above.

provinces.name: Thạch Lâu
provinces.lore: Forest climbing into high mountain near a thousand metres. Its people herd goats and gather herbs. The burned pavilion of Lăng Tiêu Các stands high on the mountain.

provinces.name: Ma Bố
provinces.lore: High forest where villagers grow hemp and weave cloth. Its people farm and weave. Hemlock forest climbs the mountain above.

provinces.name: Lâm Khẩu
provinces.lore: Forest climbing into hills, its village at the forest's mouth. Its people hunt and gather. Sabre-toothed cats roam a ridge nearby.

provinces.name: Vân Biên
provinces.lore: High forest and rock near the clouds. Its people herd goats and gather herbs. Hawks nest on a crag, and the cliff-cut halls of Đoạn Vân Viện stand broken nearby.

provinces.name: Hổ Bối Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountain and forest around Hổ Khiếu Cương. No one lives here now; the tiger and the thin ore drove the miners out. Tùng Đào's riders go around the ridges, not over them.

provinces.name: Thương Lô Trạch
provinces.lore: Swamp and forest on the northern coast, thick with grey reeds. No one lives here. Mud dragons hold its shoals.

provinces.name: Tầng Điền
provinces.lore: High forest and rock where villagers farm terraces on the slopes. Its people grow barley and buckwheat. The sealed abbey of Cô Hạc Quán stands high above.

provinces.name: Cao Hàn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest mountains of the basin, rising to nearly two thousand metres. No one lives here but miners. From its peak the whole river can be seen.

provinces.name: Tùng Tâm
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest in the north of the basin. Its people gather pine heartwood for torches. Porcupines roam a wood nearby.

provinces.name: Ô Bồng
provinces.lore: Forest and swamp on the coast, where villagers fish from boats with black awnings. Its people fish and gather reeds. A flooded wood lies behind the village.

provinces.name: Băng Thảo Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra on the northern coast, its grass frozen most of the year. No one lives here. A vein of water qi lies under the ice.

provinces.name: Bạch Thạch
provinces.lore: Forest on the coast, its village built of white stone. Its people fish and quarry. Blue martens roam the woods.

provinces.name: Đà Công
provinces.lore: River forest where villagers serve as helmsmen for Lãng Đào's ferries. Its people know every bend of the river. Weeping willows line its banks.

provinces.name: Ngọa Ngưu
provinces.lore: River forest named for a hill shaped like a resting ox. Its people farm and fish. The fallen gate of Phân Thủy Môn stands in the woods.

provinces.name: Hải Tùng
provinces.lore: Low forest coast of pines that grow right down to the shingle. A few fishing families and resin tappers live here, and their boats sell catch and pitch at Khai Dương. Inland the black pines grow so close that the coast road has never been cut through them.

provinces.name: Mục Dương
provinces.lore: Forest on the lower slopes, open steppe above and a knot of bare mountain to the west. Shepherds drive their flocks up to the summer grass and down to the woods for winter. They say their grandfathers' grandfathers found the high ground warm under snow, as the first shepherds of Dao Quang did.

provinces.name: Lâm Khẩu
provinces.lore: A wide, dark forest of the inner ridges with no river, crossed by timber tracks. Woodcutters and charcoal-burners live at its edges and seldom go deep, for the boars of the high woods are big and short-tempered. In the middle stand the burned walls of Tùng Chi Trấn, the resin town lost to fire.

provinces.name: Nhân Sâm
provinces.lore: Broad forest of the ridge country, rising to spruce woods on the higher ground. Its people dig wild ginseng and other roots under the trees and sell them to Thiên Xu's alchemists at Khai Dương. Root diggers keep their patches secret even from their own children until they are too old to climb.

provinces.name: Hữu Bật Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Right Assistant Star
provinces.lore: Steep mountains with a strip of forest along a river, empty but for hunters and patrols. It is named for the hidden star said to stand beside the Dipper, as the Phụ Tinh stands on the other side. Herb hunters climb its cold ridges for mountain flowers, and the Pivot's patrols pass through on the way to Tinh Tủy Mạch.

provinces.name: Sương Kích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High ice-capped mountains dropping straight into the northern sea, with no farmland and no village. It takes its name from the rusted iron stakes on Phụ Tinh Phong, where Phá Quân Môn drilled at night, which the frost coats white every winter. Only Thiên Xu's patrols and a few bold herb hunters come here.

provinces.name: Phóng Mã
provinces.lore: Forested hills with open steppe glades where horses are turned out to graze. Its people breed sturdy forest horses for Thiên Xu's couriers and the northern road. Wolf packs hunt the wooded ridges east of the pastures, and the herders ride in pairs.

provinces.name: Tùng Yên
provinces.lore: Rough upland of forest, steppe and red badland gullies at the southern edge of the forests. Its people burn pine in closed kilns for soot and press it into the ink sticks Thiên Xu's clerks write with. Great bears live in the high woods, and ink-makers leave a cake of honey at the forest edge each autumn.

provinces.name: Lý Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest and mountain flank along a river that comes down from the high ranges. Villagers fish the river for carp and float timber down it. A vein of Wood and Metal qi in the woods above the village draws the Pivot's ironworkers, who come to temper tools there.

provinces.name: Lộc Tồn Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Lộc Tồn Star
provinces.lore: Forested mountains along a river, named for the third of the Dipper's star-lords in Thiên Xu's reckoning. No village stands here; miners come up the river to the red iron diggings and go down again before the snow. Its cockscomb peak is a landmark for crane riders.

provinces.name: Trường Canh Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountains of black rock below Trích Tinh Phong, where the evening star is first seen over the ridge. Nothing grows here but lichen, and no one lives here but the guard of Tinh Tủy Mạch. The guard has stood since 470 and was doubled in 1188; its fires are the only lights on the ridge at night.

provinces.name: Lưu Mộc
provinces.lore: Deep river forest in the west of the ridge country. Its people fell timber and float it down the river to the coast in great rafts each spring. Walnut groves on the drier ground give them a second harvest in the autumn.

provinces.name: Chiên Mao
provinces.lore: Open steppe and thin forest above red badlands on the southern edge of Dao Quang. Herders keep sheep and goats and beat their wool into felt for tents and boots. An Earth vein lies under the steppe nearby, and its warm ground keeps the grass green into winter.

provinces.name: Liêm Trinh Nguyên
provinces.gloss: Plain of the Liêm Trinh Star
provinces.lore: Broken country of steppe, mountain, forest and badland named for the fifth of the Dipper's star-lords. Nobody farms it; herders pass through in summer, and prospectors come for the Metal vein hidden in its woods. The land is dry and the springs are few and far apart.

provinces.name: Vũ Khúc Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Vũ Khúc Star
provinces.lore: High forested mountains named for the Dipper's warrior star. In Phá Quân Môn's day its forts watched the southern roads, and their walls still stand on the heights. Today only woodcutters and patrols climb it, and they do not camp in the old forts.

provinces.name: Tham Lang Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Tham Lang Star
provinces.lore: Steep mountains and forest on the eastern side of the ranges, named for the first of the Dipper's star-lords. Lead and silver are dug here by a few hard crews. In 871 Thiên Xu camped here to besiege Phá Quân Môn, and the siege lines can still be traced on the slopes.

provinces.name: Văn Khúc Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Văn Khúc Star
provinces.lore: Tall bare mountains named for the Dipper's star of letters. Tin is dug on its lower slopes and carried down to the coast. Scholars of the Pivot climb its brush-rest peak to compose poems, and most of the poems are about how cold it is.

provinces.name: Thiên Thê Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The high spine of Dao Quang, crowned by Trích Tinh Phong and its thousand rock-cut steps. Pilgrims climb the stair all summer; no one lives here but the keepers of a few rest huts. On a shoulder below the summit lie the broken gate and walls of Phá Quân Môn.

provinces.name: Hàn Đẩu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A wall of glaciered peaks east of Trích Tinh Phong, part of the same massif. White jade is cut from the rock high on its flanks, in a short summer season. Herders say the Dipper hangs lowest over these peaks in winter, as if it had come down to rest.

provinces.name: Hồng Thạch Câu
provinces.lore: Red badland gullies and bare mountain south of the forests. Copper is dug from the red rock, and the copper crews are the only people here. Rain is rare, and when it comes the gullies run red with mud for a day.

provinces.name: Bằng Dực Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountain and badland under the cliffs of Bằng Sào Nhai, where a roc nests. No one lives here, and herders keep their flocks well away. Lodestone is dug on the ridge by crews who work under rock overhangs, out of sight of the sky.

provinces.name: Hoang Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: Stepped badland terraces and low mountain at the southern edge of Dao Quang. The ground is too dry to farm, and only herders cross it in spring when the grass comes. Its stone drum peak is said to boom when storms come off the heartland.

provinces.name: Mộc Nhĩ
provinces.lore: Damp forest along a river, thick with old logs and fungus. Its people gather wood-ear and other mushrooms and dry them on racks for the markets of Khai Dương. The red pine woods on the high ground are tapped for resin by the same families.

provinces.name: Mặc Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Dark mountains and forest whose black slate splits into fine inkstones. A small quarry crew cuts the slate and sends it to Thiên Xu's clerks and scholars. No farms stand here; the crews eat what comes up the mule path.

provinces.name: Kiều Mạch
provinces.lore: High mixed country of forest, steppe and red badland in the south-east of Dao Quang. Its people grow buckwheat on the cold upland where wheat will not ripen, and keep goats on the rest. Stone lizards bask on the badland ledges, and children are taught not to climb there.

provinces.name: Thiết Lăng Câu
provinces.lore: Sharp-edged badland ridges and mountain at the southern edge of the region. No one lives here, but turquoise is dug from the copper-stained rock and carried north. The gullies are bitter cold at night and hot by noon.

provinces.name: Liệt Thạch Câu
provinces.lore: Mountain and badland where frost has split the rock into fields of broken blocks. It is empty of people and nearly empty of water. Travellers crossing to the heartland follow the cairns and do not leave them.

provinces.name: Ẩn Lộc Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forested mountain with high grassy clearings on the southern ranges. Deer that leave the park at Lộc Uyển are said to come here to die, and hunters will not shoot in its woods. Herb gatherers come up in summer and sleep in bark huts.

provinces.name: Hải Đê
provinces.lore: Low forest coast, part of it lying below the level of the sea behind an old earth dike. Its people farm and fish behind the dike and keep it in repair together each autumn. Inland, the wind off the sea has bent the pines flat to the ground.

provinces.name: Tạo Chu
provinces.lore: Forest coast west of Khai Dương, where the firs grow tall and straight down to a sheltered bay. Its people build boats and ships of fir and sell them along the northern coast. The yards work under Khai Dương's merchants, and every keel is blessed facing the dawn.

provinces.name: Mật Phong
provinces.lore: Wide forested hills in the west of Dao Quang, with no great river. Its people keep bees in log hives and sell honey and wax as far as Thạch Kiều Thành. A Wood vein lies in the hills, and the bees that forage near it make a honey prized by alchemists.

provinces.name: Thán Diêu
provinces.lore: Forested hills between the western woods and the coast, smoky with charcoal kilns. Its people burn oak and poplar into charcoal for the smiths of Khai Dương and Thanh Bách. They cut in a ring and let each part of the forest grow back for twenty years.

provinces.name: Cự Môn
provinces.lore: Forest coast backed by the first steep mountains of the east, named for the second of the Dipper's star-lords. Its town ships timber and ore and serves the patrols bound for the high ranges. Above the town stand the empty streets of Hắc Thạch Trấn, a mining town of Phá Quân Môn that was never resettled.

provinces.name: Kình Bối Nhai
provinces.lore: Steep mountains that rise straight out of the northern sea in long humped cliffs. There is no anchorage and no farmland, only seabirds and wind. Fishermen of Cự Môn read the weather by the cloud on its tide-watching peak.

provinces.name: Cực Băng Nguyên
provinces.gloss: Ice Plain at the World's End
provinces.lore: A flat tongue of glacier at the very top of the continent, pushed into a frozen sea. No one lives here; the ice cracks too often to camp on. Băng Tâm sends novices here for a night alone to see if the cold breaks them.

provinces.name: Tùng Chi
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest on low ground, far from the sea. Its people tap the pines for resin, which they boil into pitch and sell for boats and torches. A strong Wood vein lies under the oldest stand of trees.

provinces.name: Băng Võng
provinces.lore: Fir forest on a cold coast where the sea freezes close to shore every winter. Its fishers set nets under the ice and live on the catch. The ruin of a small abbey stands in the woods inland.

provinces.name: Sương Trạch Hoang
provinces.lore: Birch woods, frozen bog and tundra run to a bleak shore. It is empty now; the fur town on its coast was given up when the sable were gone. Hunters cross it in winter when the bogs bear weight.

provinces.name: Hải Báo
provinces.lore: Wind-bent forest on a coast of low rocks where seals haul out. Its people hunt seals for oil, meat and hide, and they sell the oil as lamp fuel as far as Hòe Âm. Some tundra and bog lie behind the village.

provinces.name: Côn Bố
provinces.lore: Low coastal forest on ground that sinks below the sea in places. Its people cut kelp from the cold shallows and dry it on racks, eating it and selling it as fodder and medicine. The drowned wood inland floods every spring.

provinces.name: Hàm Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest and fog-bound swamp on the west coast. Its people salt and dry cod for the long winter and for Băng Tâm's tax. The mist of the swamp woods is so thick that the village rings a bell at dusk to call its people home.

provinces.name: Phiệt Mộc
provinces.lore: Fir forest and swamp along a sheltered shore. Its people fell timber and float it down the coast in great rafts to Hòe Âm and beyond. A great elk lives in the woods behind the village, and loggers cut around its paths.

provinces.name: Hải Nhai Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short range drops straight into the eastern sea in cliffs. No one lives here now, but iron is dug where the rock meets the water. A ruined fort on the cliffs once watched for pirates.

provinces.name: Thanh Hàn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forested foothills and bare ridges with a clear river running to the sea. Nobody farms it; hunters from Hòe Âm work its slopes. The old pines on its cliffs are said to be older than Băng Tâm.

provinces.name: U Nguyệt Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountains over the eastern coast, home to Băng Phách Mạch, the Ice Soul vein. Băng Tâm keeps the land empty except for its vein keepers and a moonstone mine. Ice beasts drawn by the vein's cold roam the passes.

provinces.name: Tuyết Giác Hoang
provinces.lore: A small cape of glacier ending in a single white hill above the sea. Nothing grows and nothing is mined. Seal hunters use the hill as a sea mark and do not land.

provinces.name: Tích Tuyết Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains rising from the coast where snow lies deep until midsummer. Cold iron is mined in a single shaft, and the miners winter at Hoàng Oanh. Nothing else lives here but goats.

provinces.name: Liệt Phong Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains where the wind off the sea never stops. A stockade from Hồ Thiên's age lies in the lower pass. No one lives here, and Băng Tâm disciples come only to train in the wind.

provinces.name: Hàn Khê
provinces.lore: A river valley of maple and fir between the mountains. Its people fish trout, burn charcoal and grow a little barley on the warm slopes. It is the last farming valley before the high ice.

provinces.name: Thương Sam Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Grey fir forest climbs to bare rock here. Silver is mined at the foot of the ridge. No village stands in it; the miners come from Hàn Khê.

provinces.name: Băng Hà Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains where slow glaciers grind down into the valleys. A Băng Tâm fort that once guarded the road to Băng Phách Mạch lies broken in the pass. The land is empty.

provinces.name: Ngân Tuyết Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains whose snow shines silver at dusk. An ice-crystal cavern is worked in the lower rock. Only miners and a few Băng Tâm sword cultivators stay here, and only in summer.

provinces.name: Vân Tiêu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A wall of high mountains rising almost from the western shore to nearly four thousand metres. Tin is mined in the low valleys. No one lives above the clouds.

provinces.name: Lam Hỏa Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with a small volcanic heart, where Hàn Diễm Khẩu breathes cold blue flame through the glacier. Alchemists come for its heat and leave quickly. The ice here is treacherous, and no one lives on it.

provinces.name: Hàn Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountains in the heart of the range. Silver is mined at the edge of the ice. No one lives here; the cold splits stone in a single night.

provinces.name: Đoạn Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains where the clouds from the sea break on the summits. A lodestone mine is worked here for compass needles and formation plates. No one stays the winter.

provinces.name: Vĩnh Đống Nguyên
provinces.lore: A broad sheet of ice that climbs from the shore to a lone summit. It has never thawed in living memory, and no one lives on it. Ice cultivators of Băng Tâm walk out here to sit where the Water qi is purest and the wind is worst.

provinces.name: Cửu Chuyển Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains around Hồi Lộ Phong and its winding ice stair. No one lives here. Băng Tâm disciples climb the stair roped together, and the ridge is named for its turns.

provinces.name: Tuyệt Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Sheer high mountains above the desert side of the range. A gold vein is worked high on the rock, and a pass fort lies buried by snow. No one lives here.

provinces.name: Vọng Tinh Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the border with Thiên Xu's land, looking down on the wild vein Tinh Tủy Mạch. No one lives here, and Băng Tâm has kept its people off the ridge since its claim to the vein was rejected in 1188. An agate cavern is still worked on the near side.

provinces.name: Băng Giản Câu
provinces.lore: Mountains cut by an icy river that runs down toward the desert, with red rock at their southern foot. Copper is mined in the gully. A beacon fort broken in the Desert Road War still stands on a spur.

provinces.name: Vạn Nhận Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains falling to the southern sea in great cliffs. No one lives here and no road crosses it. Seabirds nest on its walls in their thousands.

provinces.name: Chúc Âm Nguyên
provinces.lore: Glacier and black lava fields lie around the cone of Chúc Long Sơn, with a frozen lake and its coiled flood-dragon beyond. Hồ Thiên Phái stood here until the eruption of 425 buried it; since then the land has been empty. Băng Tâm holds it and forbids digging, and since the mountain rumbled in 1199 even the ice hunters stay away.

provinces.name: Hàn Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: A small spur of ice and moss tundra on the north coast. Reindeer cross it in summer, and a few hunters follow them. In winter it is left to the wind.

provinces.name: Sóc Phong Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat moss tundra along the northern shore, swept by the north wind for most of the year. The only people are hunters who come for fur and walrus ivory in summer. A broken city of Hồ Thiên's age lies on its coast, and a frozen Water vein lies inland.

provinces.name: Tuyết Tùng Lâm
provinces.lore: Stunted pine forest thins out here into open tundra. No village stands in it, because the snow owls of the plain take lambs, dogs and sometimes children. Trappers from Hàn Trạch work its edges in winter.

provinces.name: Hàn Trạch
provinces.lore: Fir forest broken by wide peat bogs on the edge of the tundra. Its people cut peat for fuel, pick cranberries and trap fur, and they sell all three to the coast. It is the northernmost village that pays Băng Tâm's tax in coin rather than fish.

provinces.name: Lạc Tuyết Nguyên
provinces.lore: Half fir forest and half open tundra, where snow falls on more days than not. No one lives here, but a Wood vein in the forest draws Băng Tâm's herb gatherers in summer. The coast is low and drowned in ice for half the year.

provinces.name: Xích Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Red-rocked mountains between the ice range and the desert. No one lives here now; turquoise is mined in the hills. The burned stockade of Dạ Quang's raider days still stands in a side valley.

provinces.name: Hoàng Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Dry steppe that turns into open dunes in the south. No village stands here; caravans cross it in two days and do not stop. Golden scorpions hunt in the dunes.

provinces.name: Sạn Đạo Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains, badlands and desert cut by the gorge of Viên Đề Hạp and its plank road. No sect holds the road and no one lives here; caravans cross with wax in their ears. Copper-red rock and dry slopes surround the gorge.

provinces.name: Hãn Hải Mạc
provinces.lore: Open desert with a few bare hills and badland ridges. No one lives here but at a boiling spring in the sand, where caravans water their beasts. Băng Tâm keeps a cairn of water jars there for travellers.

provinces.name: Lưu Sa Câu
provinces.lore: Desert cut by a thin river whose bed shifts every year. Wild camels graze the river edge, and no one settles here. Caravans follow the river and pay for guides who know where the sand is soft.

provinces.name: Chiên Trướng
provinces.lore: Wide steppe with some desert and badland to the south. Its herders live in felt tents, move with their flocks and make felt for the seat and the caravans. A Fire vein lies in the desert edge.

provinces.name: Chử Diêm
provinces.lore: Coastal steppe running down to a salt shore. Its people boil sea water into salt over dung fires and sell it to the caravans and to Hồi Lan. A bitter hot spring rises inland.

provinces.name: Hàn Tùng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Pine-covered mountains on the north edge of the desert. Coal is dug here for the seat's forges. The ruin of a small sect that died in the Desert Road War lies in the pines.

provinces.name: Mộc Kiều
provinces.lore: A river valley of forest and steppe below the mountains. Its people log, farm a little and keep the timber bridge on the road from the seat to the coast. Silver foxes live in the woods above.

provinces.name: Ngọc Môn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Very high mountains, over four and a half thousand metres, at the west end of the desert. White jade is mined at their foot. The old poem of Cô Thành looks toward the jade gate, and caravan drivers say this is it.

provinces.name: Đà Linh
provinces.lore: Steppe and desert along a river under the mountains, where caravans gather before the long crossing. Camel breeders, harness makers and innkeepers live in its town. A sandstorm-swept Earth vein lies to the west.

provinces.name: Lạc Nhật Nguyên
provinces.lore: Half steppe and half desert along a long river, where the lone smoke of caravan fires rises straight in still air. No one settles here. A Fire vein lies where the sun sets over the river.

provinces.name: Mục Dương
provinces.lore: Steppe with patches of desert and red badland in the east. Its people herd sheep and goats and sell wool to the seat and to Hồi Lan. An Earth vein lies under a low rise.

provinces.name: Tuyết Hải Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Huge mountains with small glaciers rise over the west of the desert. No one lives here. The empty fort of Băng Tâm's first ice keepers stands in a pass.

provinces.name: Liệt Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and red badlands split by heat and frost. No one lives here, and the old caravan fort lies under sand. Snakes and scorpions shelter in the cracks.

provinces.name: Thiên Bắc Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra, glacier and bare rock at the northern tip of the frost coast. No one lives here now. A city of Hàn Giang's age lies empty on the shore.

provinces.name: Chưng Vụ Lĩnh
